14: # Skill Reference File Templates - AI Agent Skills
15: 
16: Templates for creating reference files in AI agent skills with deep-dive technical guidance.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Location & Naming
23: 
24: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/references/`
25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only
27: 
28: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
29: |---------------|-----------------|
30: | `implementation-workflows.md` | `ImplementationWorkflows.md` (PascalCase) |
31: | `tool-catalog.md` | `tool_catalog.md` (snake_case) |
32: | `debugging-guide.md` | `DebuggingGuide.MD` (wrong case) |
33: | `quick-reference.md` | `quickReference.md` (camelCase) |
34: | `code-quality-standards.md` | `code quality standards.md` (spaces) |
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```
67: 
68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
69: 
70: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
71: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.
72: 
73: #### GOOD Intro Structure
74: 
75: ```markdown
76: # Git Commit Workflows
77: 
78: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: \## 1. OVERVIEW
83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
86: 
87: ### When to Use
88: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
89: - Filtering generated files from commits
90: - Writing clear commit messages
91: 
92: ### Core Principle
93: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
94: ```
95: 
96: #### BAD Intro Structure (duplicates content)
97: 
98: ```markdown
99: # Git Commit Workflows
100: 
101: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
102: 
103: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!
104: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
105: 
106: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
107: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
108: 
109: ---
110: 
111: \## 1. OVERVIEW
112: 
113: ### Purpose
114: Provides systematic workflows...  ← Now this duplicates the intro!
115: 
116: ### Core Principle
117: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!
118: ```
119: 
120: #### Intro vs Section 1 Content Placement
121: 
122: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | Section 1 OVERVIEW |
123: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ |
124: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat) |
125: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
126: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
127: | Primary Sources       | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (as "Key Sources") |
128: | Purpose (detailed)    | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
129: | Prerequisites         | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
130: | Any H3 subsections    | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES              |
131: 
132: ---
133: 
134: ### Reference Body Skeleton
135: 
136: **Every reference body follows this order.** The hook and the Purpose say different things: the hook names the job, and the Purpose names the outcome.
137: 
138: ```markdown
139: # [Title]
140: 
141: [1-2 sentence hook: what this reference covers and when to reach for it.]
142: 
143: ---
144: 
145: ## 1. OVERVIEW
146: 
147: ### Purpose
148: 
149: [The outcome this reference produces, in one or two sentences.]
150: 
151: ### When to Use
152: 
153: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
154: - [Second trigger]
155: 
156: ### Core Principle
157: 
158: [One-line statement that governs every rule below.]
159: 
160: ### Boundaries
161: 
162: - **In scope**: [What this reference owns]
163: - **Out of scope**: [What belongs in a sibling reference]
164: 
165: ### Key Sources
166: 
167: - [title](url) - [What the source establishes]
168: 
169: ---
170: 
171: ## 2. [CONTENT SECTION]
172: 
173: ### [Rule Group]
174: 
175: - **Rule:** [What to do]
176: - **Why:** [The failure it prevents]
177: - **Check:** [How to verify it]
178: 
179: ---
180: 
181: ## 3. [CONTENT SECTION]
182: 
183: [Body of the section]
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ## 4. RELATED RESOURCES
188: 
189: - [title](./sibling-reference.md) - [What the reader gets there]
190: ```
191: 
192: **Rules the skeleton encodes:**
193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.
194: - Content sections use integer numbers only: `## 2.`, `## 3.`, and so on.
195: - Rule fields are `- **Label:** text` bullets, never two bold labels on consecutive lines.
196: - Links are `[title](url)`, never a bare URL.
197: - Every `---` has a blank line above it, so a divider never turns the line above into a setext heading.
198: - A related section, when present, is the last H2.
199: 
200: ---
201: 
202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```
229: 
230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.
231: 
232: ---
233: 
234: ## 3. WHEN TO CREATE REFERENCE FILES
235: 
236: ### Create Reference File When
237: 
238: **Workflow Complexity**:
239: - Multi-phase workflows with validation checkpoints
240: - Decision trees with multiple branches
241: - Pattern libraries with 5+ variations
242: - Systematic debugging procedures
243: 
244: **Technical Depth**:
245: - Root cause analysis required
246: - Tool integration details (MCP, scripts)
247: - Before/after code transformations
248: - Common error patterns and fixes
249: 
250: **Size Threshold**:
251: - Content exceeds 200 lines
252: - Multiple related workflows
253: - Extensive troubleshooting needed
254: 
255: ### Keep in SKILL.md When
256: 
257: **Core Content**:
258: - Overview and "When to Use"
259: - High-level workflow (3-5 steps)
260: - Essential rules (ALWAYS/NEVER/ESCALATE IF)
261:   > **Note**: RULES sections in SKILL.md use ALL-CAPS H3 headers: `### ALWAYS`, `### NEVER`, `### ESCALATE IF` (or `####` at phase depth). See [skill-md-template.md](./skill-md-template.md) for the complete pattern.
262: - Quick reference
263: 
264: **Size**: Content under 200 lines
265: 
266: ### Reference File Types for AI Agent Skills
267: 
268: | Type                | Purpose                                | Example (kebab-case)          | Size           |
269: | ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------- |
270: | **Workflow**        | Multi-phase processes with checkpoints | `implementation-workflows.md` | 500-1500 lines |
271: | **Pattern Library** | Code patterns with before/after        | `shared-patterns.md`          | 300-800 lines  |
272: | **Standards**       | Rules and conventions                  | `code-quality-standards.md`   | 400-1000 lines |
273: | **Debugging**       | Systematic troubleshooting             | `debugging-workflows.md`      | 600-1200 lines |
274: | **Tool Guide**      | MCP/external tool integration          | `devtools-guide.md`           | 200-600 lines  |
275: | **Quick Reference** | Commands, shortcuts, checklists        | `quick-reference.md`          | 200-400 lines  |
276: 
277: **Note:** All authored reference file names use kebab-case (hyphens, lowercase).
278: 
279: ---
280: 
281: ## 4. AI AGENT SKILL REFERENCE CHARACTERISTICS
282: 
283: ### Core Principle Statements
284: 
285: **Purpose**: Distill philosophy into one-line wisdom
286: 
287: > **PLACEMENT**: Core Principle goes in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph after the H1 title.
288: 
289: **Format**:
290: ```markdown
291: \## 1. OVERVIEW
292: 
293: ### Purpose
294: 
295: [The outcome this reference produces]
296: 
297: ### When to Use
298: 
299: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
300: 
301: ### Core Principle
302: 
303: [Single powerful statement that captures the workflow's essence]
304: ```
305: 
306: **Examples from Real Skills**:
307: - "Wait for the actual condition you care about, not a guess about how long it takes"
308: - "ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure"
309: - "Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history"
310: 
311: ### Phased Workflows with Validation
312: 
313: **Purpose**: Structured processes with mandatory checkpoints
314: 
315: **Format**:
316: ```markdown
317: ### The [Number] Phases
318: 
319: You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
320: 
321: #### Phase 1: [Phase Name]
322: 
323: **Purpose**: [What this phase accomplishes]
324: 
325: **Actions**:
326: 1. [Action 1]
327: 2. [Action 2]
328: 
329: **Validation**: `checkpoint_name`
330: 
331: #### Phase 2: [Phase Name]
332: 
333: [Similar structure]
334: ```
335: 
336: **Key Elements**:
337: - **"You MUST complete"** - Mandatory language
338: - **Named checkpoints** - `checkpoint_name` for validation
339: - **Sequential phases** - Cannot skip ahead
340: 
341: ### Before/After Code Examples
342: 
343: **Purpose**: Show transformation from wrong to right
344: 
345: **Format**:
346: ```markdown
347: ### [Pattern Name]
348: 
349: **BEFORE**: [Problem description]
350: \```[language]
351: // Bad code with issues
352: // Showing what NOT to do
353: \```
354: 
355: **AFTER**: [Solution description]
356: \```[language]
357: // Good code with fixes
358: // Showing correct approach
359: \```
360: 
361: **Why better**: [Explanation of improvement]
362: ```
363: 
364: **Key Elements**:
365: - `BEFORE:` marker for the wrong-way code
366: - `AFTER:` marker for the right-way code
367: - Inline comments explaining issues
368: - "Why better" rationale
369: 
370: ### Pattern Comparison Tables
371: 
372: **Purpose**: Compare approaches across scenarios
373: 
374: **Format**:
375: ```markdown
376: ### Common Patterns
377: 
378: | Scenario     | Approach A (Wrong) | Approach B (Right) | Why Better  |
379: | ------------ | ------------------ | ------------------ | ----------- |
380: | [Scenario 1] | [Wrong way]        | [Right way]        | [Rationale] |
381: | [Scenario 2] | [Wrong way]        | [Right way]        | [Rationale] |
382: ```
383: 
384: **Use when**: Multiple scenarios need comparison
385: 
386: ### Decision Logic in Markdown
387: 
388: **Purpose**: Explicit if/then logic for workflow decisions
389: 
390: **Format**:
391: \```markdown
392: ### Decision Logic
393: 
394: \```markdown
395: IF [condition A]:
396:   → [Action/Path A]
397:   → [Expected outcome A]
398: 
399: IF [condition B]:
400:   → [Action/Path B]
401:   → [Expected outcome B]
402: 
403: IF [condition C]:
404:   → [Action/Path C]

407: \```

415: │     └─ Expected outcome A

417: │  └─ Execute Workflow B
418: │     └─ Expected outcome B

426: 
427: **Purpose**: Named checkpoints throughout workflows
428: 
429: **Format**:

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766: 
767: ---
768: 
769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882: 
883: ---
884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006: 
1007: ---
1008: 
1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"
1073:

21: 
22: ### Location & Naming

25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only

38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```
67: 
68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.

70: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
71: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.

73: #### GOOD Intro Structure
74: 
75: ```markdown
76: # Git Commit Workflows
77: 
78: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: \## 1. OVERVIEW
83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
86: 
87: ### When to Use
88: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
89: - Filtering generated files from commits
90: - Writing clear commit messages
91: 
92: ### Core Principle
93: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
94: ```
95:

98: ```markdown

100: 
101: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
102: 
103: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!

105: 
106: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
107: - Creating commits with multiple file changes

109: ---
110: 
111: \## 1. OVERVIEW
112: 
113: ### Purpose
114: Provides systematic workflows...  ← Now this duplicates the intro!
115: 
116: ### Core Principle
117: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!

193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.

202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```
229: 
230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.

245: - Root cause analysis required

253: - Extensive troubleshooting needed

262: - Quick reference

264: **Size**: Content under 200 lines

281: ## 4. AI AGENT SKILL REFERENCE CHARACTERISTICS
282: 
283: ### Core Principle Statements
284: 
285: **Purpose**: Distill philosophy into one-line wisdom
286: 
287: > **PLACEMENT**: Core Principle goes in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph after the H1 title.
288: 
289: **Format**:
290: ```markdown
291: \## 1. OVERVIEW
292: 
293: ### Purpose
294: 
295: [The outcome this reference produces]
296: 
297: ### When to Use
298: 
299: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
300: 
301: ### Core Principle
302: 
303: [Single powerful statement that captures the workflow's essence]
304: ```
305: 
306: **Examples from Real Skills**:
307: - "Wait for the actual condition you care about, not a guess about how long it takes"
308: - "ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure"
309: - "Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history"
310: 
311: ### Phased Workflows with Validation
312: 
313: **Purpose**: Structured processes with mandatory checkpoints
314: 
315: **Format**:
316: ```markdown
317: ### The [Number] Phases
318: 
319: You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
320: 
321: #### Phase 1: [Phase Name]
322: 
323: **Purpose**: [What this phase accomplishes]
324: 
325: **Actions**:
326: 1. [Action 1]
327: 2. [Action 2]
328: 
329: **Validation**: `checkpoint_name`

332: 
333: [Similar structure]
334: ```

337: - **"You MUST complete"** - Mandatory language
338: - **Named checkpoints** - `checkpoint_name` for validation
339: - **Sequential phases** - Cannot skip ahead

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766:

769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882:

884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006:

1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"

15: # Gantt Chart
16: 
17: ## 1. OVERVIEW
18: 
19: **Best for:** project plans and roadmaps — tasks with explicit start and end dates, grouped into phases. Use when the reader needs to see temporal overlap, parallel tracks, and milestone sequencing at a glance.
20: 
21: ---
22: 
23: ## 2. LAYOUT CONVENTIONS
24: 
25: - **Left label column:** x=20–200 (180px). Task names in Geist sans 11px 600. Phase labels as Geist Mono 7px eyebrows above each group.
26: - **Timeline area:** x=200–960 (760px). Time axis runs left→right.
27: - **Row height:** 40px per task. Each bar occupies h=24px centered in the row (8px top padding).
28: - **Time axis:** Geist Mono 8px week/month labels at x=200+i×pitch, y=56 (just above first task row). A hairline separator at y=64.
29: - **Phase grouping:** a subtle zone rect (same pattern as architecture zone) behind each phase's rows, with an eyebrow label in the top-left margin. Use `rgba(45,49,66,0.02)` fill, `rgba(45,49,66,0.10)` stroke.
30: - **Focal task bar:** 1 bar in accent fill/stroke (the key deliverable or critical path task). All others: muted fill @ 0.15, muted stroke.
31: - **Today / milestone marker:** optional vertical dashed line in `muted` at the current week x-position.
32: 
33: ### Task bar pattern
34: 
35: ```svg
36: <!-- Non-focal task -->
37: <rect x="X_start" y="ROW_Y+8" width="DURATION_PX" height="24" rx="4"
38:       fill="rgba(79,93,117,0.15)" stroke="#4f5d75" stroke-width="1"/>
39: <text x="X_start+8" y="ROW_Y+25" fill="#2d3142" font-size="10" font-weight="600"
40:       font-family="'Geist', sans-serif">Task name</text>
41: 
42: <!-- Focal task -->
43: <rect x="X_start" y="ROW_Y+8" width="DURATION_PX" height="24" rx="4"
44:       fill="rgba(235,108,54,0.12)" stroke="#eb6c36" stroke-width="1"/>
45: <text x="X_start+8" y="ROW_Y+25" fill="#eb6c36" font-size="10" font-weight="600"
46:       font-family="'Geist', sans-serif">Key task</text>
47: ```
48: 
49: Duration in pixels: `(end_week - start_week) × pitch`. Pitch = timeline_width / total_weeks.
50: 
51: ---
52: 
53: ## 3. ANTI-PATTERNS
54: 
55: - More than 12 tasks (splits into sub-plans or collapses into phase-level view).
56: - More than 5 parallel tracks per phase (illegible overlap).
57: - Dependency arrows between tasks in v1 (add only when essential; use the annotation primitive for labels).
58: - Start/end dates in the bar label (put them in the x-axis or tooltip comment instead).
59: - Equal visual weight for all bars (the focal task must stand out).
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: ## 4. EXAMPLES
64: 
65: - `assets/diagrams/gantt.html` — minimal light
66: - `assets/diagrams/gantt-dark.html` — minimal dark
67: - `assets/diagrams/gantt-full.html` — full editorial

14: ---
15: 
16: # High-Level
17: 
18: ## 1. OVERVIEW
19: 
20: **Best for:** end-to-end data stack overviews — ingestion → storage → query → analytics → visualization — deployed on a container orchestrator (Kubernetes, ECS, Nomad). Combines a phase chevron banner, deployment boundary, orchestration bar, identity footer, and (optionally) a right-side vertical chevron strip for cross-cutting concerns (Orchestration, Security, Observability).
21: 
22: This type is **parametric**. The diagram is fully determined by a small list of inputs (chevrons, sources, components, connections). The formulas below tell you exactly where every shape lands given those inputs — two generations from the same inputs must produce visually identical SVG.
23: 
24: ---
25: 
26: ## 2. INPUTS — THE PARAMETER CONTRACT
27: 
28: Before drawing, collect these from the user (or accept them as a YAML/JSON block). Everything in this reference is derived from these inputs. Don't invent geometry on the fly.
29: 
30: ```yaml
31: chevrons:                       # ordered left → right; reserved names auto-promote to vertical
32:   - { name: "Data sources",         columns: 1 }
33:   - { name: "Ingestion",            columns: 1 }
34:   - { name: "Storage",              columns: 1 }
35:   - { name: "Transformation",       columns: 1 }
36:   - { name: "Visualization",        columns: 1 }
37:   - { name: "Orchestration",        vertical: true }                     # reserved → pairs with the bar
38:   - { name: "Security",             vertical: true, color: "#b85450" }   # tinted to match the Identity bar below
39:   - { name: "Observability",        vertical: true }                     # reserved → pairs with crosscut #2
40: 
41: sources:                        # external; rendered in the dashed zone on the left
42:   - { name: "PostgreSQL", type: "db",     connects_to: ["NiFi"] }
43:   - { name: "SFTP drop",  type: "ftp",    connects_to: ["NiFi"] }
44:   - { name: "Web forms",  type: "web",    connects_to: ["NiFi"] }
45:   - { name: "Legacy",     type: "legacy", connects_to: ["NiFi"] }
46: 
47: components:                     # inside the cluster, plus bars and cross-cutting rows
48:   - { name: "NiFi",       chevron: "Ingestion",      kind: node,          icon: nifi,     role: "COLL"  }
49:   - { name: "MinIO",      chevron: "Storage",        kind: node,          icon: minio,    role: "STORE", focal: true }
50:   - { name: "Trino",      chevron: "Storage",        kind: node,          icon: trino,    role: "VIRT"  }
51:   - { name: "Notebooks",  chevron: "Transformation", kind: node,          icon: jupyter,  role: "ANLZ"  }
52:   - { name: "Superset",   chevron: "Visualization",  kind: node,          icon: superset, role: "DASH" }
53:   - { name: "Airflow",    chevron: "Orchestration",  kind: bar,           icon: airflow,    subtitle: "Apache Airflow" }
54:   - { name: "Identity",   chevron: "Security",       kind: cross-cutting, icon: keycloak,   subtitle: "Keycloak · LDAP · OIDC",     color: "#b85450" }
55:   - { name: "Monitoring", chevron: "Observability",  kind: cross-cutting, icon: prometheus, subtitle: "Prometheus · Grafana · Loki" }
56: 
57: connections:                    # explicit edges; focal-touching ones become accent automatically
58:   - { from: "NiFi",    to: "MinIO",                style: "primary" }
59:   - { from: "NiFi",    to: "Trino",                style: "secondary" }
60:   - { from: "MinIO",   to: "Notebooks",            style: "primary" }
61:   - { from: "Trino",   to: "MinIO",                style: "query" }   # read-back (dashed)
62:   - { from: "Notebooks", to: "Superset",           style: "secondary" }
63:   - { from: "Airflow", to: ["NiFi", "Trino", "Notebooks"], style: "trigger" }
64: 
65: focal: "MinIO"                  # exactly one; defaults to first kind=node under "Storage"
66: dark: false
67: ```
68: 
69: **Reserved chevron names** (always vertical, even if `vertical: true` is omitted): `Orchestration`, `Security`, `Observability`, `Governance`, `Backup`.
70: 
71: **Reserved `kind` values:**
72: - `node` — a standard box inside the cluster (default).
73: - `bar` — a horizontal strip spanning the cluster top. Typically one (Orchestration); see §6 for the pairing rule.
74: - `cross-cutting` — a horizontal strip spanning the body width (stops at the strip margin), stacked below the cluster. **Zero or more allowed**; each stacks 44 px below the previous (§3.5) and pairs 1:1 with a vertical chevron (§6).
75: 
76: **Optional `color`** (per component, hex string): tints the component's container and content while leaving connectors untouched. See §4.4. Use sparingly — a custom color is a semantic flag (e.g., red = security concern), not decoration.
77: 
78: **Source `type` values** → icon mapping (use `references/primitives/primitive-icons.md`):
79: - `db` → `database`
80: - `ftp` → `bucket` or upload arrow
81: - `web` → `internet`
82: - `legacy` → `server`
83: - `api` → `api`
84: - Any explicit icon name in `primitive-icons.md` is also accepted.
85: 
86: ---
87: 
88: ## 3. LAYOUT FORMULAS — DETERMINISTIC GEOMETRY
89: 
90: Every coordinate below is derived from the inputs. **No hardcoded numbers in examples that aren't justified here.**
91: 
92: ### 3.1 Canvas
93: 
94: ```
95: has_vertical       = any(c.vertical or c.name in reserved_names for c in chevrons)
96: right_strip_w      = 28  if has_vertical else 0
97: strip_margin       = 8   if has_vertical else 0   # gap between body and right strip
98: effective_w        = 1000 - right_strip_w - strip_margin     # 1000 or 964
99: 
100: n_cross            = count of components with kind == "cross-cutting"
101: strip_y_bot        = max(428, 388 + n_cross * 44 - 4)        # extends to last crosscut row
102: viewBox_h          = max(540, strip_y_bot + 112)             # 112 reserved for legend
103: viewBox            = f"0 0 1000 {viewBox_h}"
104: ```
105: 
106: Every horizontal element (chevron banner, cluster, orchestration bar, identity / cross-cutting bars) ends at `effective_w`. The right strip sits at `x = 1000 - right_strip_w` (= 972). The 8-px band between them is visual breathing room — never put content there.
107: 
108: `viewBox_h` grows when more than one cross-cutting bar is declared: 1 crosscut → 540, 2 → 600 (or 584 if you want it tight; the rule rounds to the next multiple of 20 for clean grids).
109: 
110: ### 3.2 Horizontal chevron banner
111: 
112: ```
113: y_banner           = 4
114: h_banner           = 28
115: horizontals        = [c for c in chevrons if not c.vertical and c.name not in reserved_names]
116: sum_columns        = sum(c.columns for c in horizontals)
117: base_unit          = floor_to_4(effective_w / sum_columns)        # multiple of 4
118: widths             = [max(120, base_unit * c.columns) for c in horizontals]
119: widths[-1]         += effective_w - sum(widths)                   # trailing absorbs remainder
120: x_boundaries       = cumulative_sum([0] + widths)                 # length sum_columns+1
121: chevron_cx(C)      = (x_boundaries[index(C)] + x_boundaries[index(C)+1]) / 2
122: ```
123: 
124: **Polygon shapes:**
125: - First (leftmost): `(x0,4) (x1-12,4) (x1,18) (x1-12,32) (x0,32)`
126: - Middle: `(x0,4) (x1-12,4) (x1,18) (x1-12,32) (x0,32) (x0+12,18)`
127: - Last (rightmost): `(x0,4) (effective_w,4) (effective_w,32) (x0,32) (x0+12,18)`
128: 
129: Fills alternate `#2d3142` / `#3d4460` (light mode) or `#3d4460` / `#4a5270` (dark mode). Labels: paper-colored mono `font-size=7`, `letter-spacing=0.14em`, `text-anchor=middle`, centered at `chevron_cx, 21`.
130: 
131: **Color override** (per chevron, both horizontal and vertical): a chevron may declare an optional `color: "#hex"` that replaces the alternation fill for that one chevron. Use it to flag a phase that pairs with a custom-colored component (e.g., `Security` chevron in red when the Identity bar uses `color: "#b85450"`). Rules:
132: 
133: - Override applies to the polygon fill only. The label stays paper-colored — never recolor chevron labels.
134: - The alternation index doesn't shift; neighboring chevrons keep their natural fill, even if it produces two adjacent same-fill chevrons. Don't try to "fix" this — overrides should be rare (≤ 2 per diagram).
135: - In dark mode, use the same hex unless contrast against paper labels suffers; if it does, pick a darker shade for dark mode and document it as a `color_dark` field on that chevron.
136: - A chevron color override is independent of any paired component's color, but pairing them (same hex on chevron + bar) is the conventional way to make the column "read" as one concern.
137: 
138: ### 3.3 Source zone (dashed, external)
139: 
140: ```
141: sources_x          = 4
142: sources_y          = 40
143: sources_w          = x_boundaries[1] - 8           # width of the first chevron, minus 4px gutter each side
144: sources_h          = 336
145: ```
146: 
147: Stroke: `rgba(45,49,66,0.20)`, `stroke-width=0.8`, `stroke-dasharray=6,3`, `rx=6`. Zone fill: `rgba(45,49,66,0.02)`.
148: 
149: ### 3.4 Cluster boundary (solid)
150: 
151: ```
152: cluster_x          = x_boundaries[1] + 4           # starts at end of source zone + 4px gutter
153: cluster_y          = 40
154: cluster_w          = effective_w - cluster_x       # extends to right strip / canvas edge
155: cluster_h          = 336
156: ```
157: 
158: Stroke: `rgba(45,49,66,0.18)`, `stroke-width=1.2`, `rx=8`. Fill: `rgba(45,49,66,0.02)`. K8s icon + label at `(cluster_x + 16, 352)` (icon) and `(cluster_x + 40, 362)` (text).
159: 
160: ### 3.5 Cross-cutting bars (identity, observability, …)
161: 
162: Zero or more `kind: cross-cutting` components stack below the cluster. Each gets its own 40-px row with a 4-px gap.
163: 
164: ```
165: crosscuts          = [c for c in components if c.kind == "cross-cutting"]   # ordered as declared
166: cross_x            = 4
167: cross_y(k)         = 388 + k * 44                  # 388, 432, 476, …
168: cross_w            = effective_w - 4               # spans body width, stops at the strip margin
169: cross_h            = 40
170: ```
171: 
172: Stroke: `rgba(45,49,66,0.20)`, `stroke-width=0.8`, `rx=6`. Fill: `rgba(45,49,66,0.05)`. Icon at `(16, cross_y(k) + 10)`, name centered at `(effective_w / 2, cross_y(k) + 22)`, subtitle at `(effective_w / 2, cross_y(k) + 34)`.
173: 
174: Reserved cross-cutting *concerns* (informational; user can name the actual bar whatever they want):
175: - **Identity / Security** — Keycloak, LDAP/AD, Okta, Auth0, OIDC providers
176: - **Observability** — Prometheus + Grafana, Datadog, OpenTelemetry, Loki
177: - **Backup / DR** — Velero, Restic, snapshot orchestrators
178: - **Governance / Lineage** — OpenMetadata, DataHub, Apache Atlas
179: - **Secrets / config** — Vault, Sealed Secrets, External Secrets
180: 
181: Each cross-cutting bar pairs 1:1 with a vertical chevron in the right strip (§6).
182: 
183: ### 3.6 Orchestration bar component (inside cluster)
184: 
185: ```
186: bar_x              = cluster_x + 12
187: bar_y              = 52
188: bar_w              = cluster_w - 24
189: bar_h              = 44
190: ```
191: 
192: Stroke: `rgba(45,49,66,0.18)`, `stroke-width=0.8`, `rx=4`. Fill: `rgba(45,49,66,0.05)`. Tool icon at the far right (`bar_x + bar_w - 50, 58`); name centered at `(bar_x + bar_w/2, 71)`; subtitle at `(bar_x + bar_w/2, 84)`.
193: 
194: ### 3.7 Component nodes (inside cluster)
195: 
196: ```
197: node_w             = 152
198: node_h             = 80                            # focal same height, accent border
199: node_cx(N)         = chevron_cx(N.chevron)         # ← non-negotiable
200: node_x(N)          = node_cx(N) - node_w/2
201: ```
202: 
203: If a chevron has K nodes assigned, stack them vertically:
204: 
205: ```
206: first_top_y        = 120 if any bar in this column else 64
207: gap                = 16
208: row_top(k)         = first_top_y + k * (node_h + gap)   # k = 0..K-1
209: ```
210: 
211: **Focal node:** `fill="rgba(235,108,54,0.08)"`, `stroke="#eb6c36"`, `stroke-width=1.2`. Title text in accent color. All other nodes: white fill, `stroke=rgba(45,49,66,0.25)`, `stroke-width=1`.
212: 
213: Role badge top-left at `(node_x+8, node_y+6)`, size 12 high. Icon top-right at `(node_x+node_w-32, node_y+6)`, 24×24, monochrome via `currentColor`. Name centered at `(node_cx, node_y+44)` size 11 sans semibold. Subtitle at `(node_cx, node_y+56)` size 8 mono muted.
214: 
215: ### 3.8 Source nodes (inside dashed zone)
216: 
217: ```
218: src_node_w         = sources_w - 8
219: src_node_h         = 64                            # uniform; chosen to fit ≤ 4 sources
220: src_node_x         = sources_x + 4
221: src_first_top_y    = 60
222: src_gap            = 16
223: src_row_top(k)     = src_first_top_y + k * (src_node_h + src_gap)
224: ```
225: 
226: Same role-badge / icon / name / subtitle pattern as cluster nodes (icon at `src_node_x+54, row_top(k)+6`; name centered at `src_node_x+src_node_w/2, row_top(k)+42`; subtitle one line below). Role badge text: `EXT`. Caps at 4 sources; for more, split into a separate diagram.
227: 
228: ### 3.9 Right strip — vertical chevrons
229: 
230: ```
231: strip_x            = 1000 - right_strip_w       # 972 when present
232: strip_w            = 28
233: verticals          = [c for c in chevrons if c.vertical or c.name in reserved_names]
234: strip_y_top        = 40
235: strip_y_bot        = max(428, 388 + n_cross * 44 - 4)   # extends to last crosscut row (see §3.1)
236: strip_h_total      = strip_y_bot - strip_y_top
237: heights            = [floor_to_4(strip_h_total / len(verticals))] * len(verticals)
238: heights[-1]       += strip_h_total - sum(heights)       # last absorbs remainder
239: ```
240: 
241: Examples:
242: - 2 verticals (Orchestration + Security), 1 crosscut → `heights = [192, 196]`, layout `[40..232, 232..428]`.
243: - 3 verticals (Orchestration + Security + Observability), 2 crosscuts → `strip_y_bot = 472`, `strip_h_total = 432`, `heights = [144, 144, 144]`, layout `[40..184, 184..328, 328..472]`.
244: 
245: Adjacent edges share the same y (no gap), like horizontal chevrons share x at their boundary.
246: 
247: **Polygon shapes** (top-to-bottom flow, mirrors horizontal §3.2):
248: - First (topmost): flat top, point at bottom — `(strip_x, y0) (strip_x+strip_w, y0) (strip_x+strip_w, y1-12) (strip_x+strip_w/2, y1) (strip_x, y1-12)`
249: - Middle: notch on top, point on bottom — `(strip_x, y0) (strip_x+strip_w/2, y0+12) (strip_x+strip_w, y0) (strip_x+strip_w, y1-12) (strip_x+strip_w/2, y1) (strip_x, y1-12)`
250: - Last (bottommost): notch on top, flat bottom — `(strip_x, y0) (strip_x+strip_w/2, y0+12) (strip_x+strip_w, y0) (strip_x+strip_w, y1) (strip_x, y1)`
251: 
252: Fills alternate `#2d3142` / `#3d4460` (same palette as horizontals). Labels: paper-colored mono `font-size=7`, `letter-spacing=0.14em`, **rotated −90°**, anchored at `(strip_x + strip_w/2, (y0+y1)/2)`.
253: 
254: Vertical chevrons honor the per-chevron `color` override documented in §3.2 — apply the hex to the polygon fill, leave the rotated label paper-colored. Pair the override with the same hex on the chevron's paired bar/crosscut to bind them visually as one concern.
255: 
256: ---
257: 
258: ## 4. CONNECTOR RULES (MANDATORY)
259: 
260: These are non-negotiable. Pick the style **automatically** from the topology — do not let the user override style on focal-touching or bar-originating edges.
261: 
262: | `style` | Stroke | Width | Dash | Marker | When required |
263: |---|---|---|---|---|---|
264: | `primary` | `#eb6c36` | 1.2 | — | `arrow-accent` | Every edge whose endpoint is the `focal` node. |
265: | `secondary` | `#4f5d75` | 1.0 | — | `arrow` | Default for source→component and component→component when neither endpoint is focal. |
266: | `trigger` | `#4f5d75` | 1.0 | `4,3` | `arrow-sm` | Every edge originating from a `kind: bar` component. |
267: | `query` | `rgba(45,49,66,0.30)` | 1.0 | `4,3` | `arrow` | Read-back edges (e.g., focal ↔ Trino). |
268: 
269: **Defs block** (required, exactly these four markers):
270: 
271: ```svg
272: <defs>
273:   <marker id="arrow"        markerWidth="8" markerHeight="6" refX="7" refY="3"   orient="auto"><polygon points="0 0, 8 3, 0 6" fill="#4f5d75"/></marker>
274:   <marker id="arrow-accent" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="6" refX="7" refY="3"   orient="auto"><polygon points="0 0, 8 3, 0 6" fill="#eb6c36"/></marker>
275:   <marker id="arrow-sm"     markerWidth="6" markerHeight="5" refX="5" refY="2.5" orient="auto"><polygon points="0 0, 6 2.5, 0 5" fill="#4f5d75"/></marker>
276:   <marker id="arrow-dim"    markerWidth="8" markerHeight="6" refX="7" refY="3"   orient="auto"><polygon points="0 0, 8 3, 0 6" fill="rgba(45,49,66,0.45)"/></marker>
277: </defs>
278: ```
279: 
280: ### 4.1 Exit / entry sides (non-negotiable)
281: 
282: | Edge kind | Exit side of source | Entry side of target |
283: |---|---|---|
284: | Source → cluster node | **right** of source node | **left** of target |
285: | Component → component (within cluster) | **right** | **left** |
286: | Bar component → node | **bottom** of bar | **top** of node |
287: | Cross-cutting bar | — (emits no edges) | — |
288: | Vertical chevron | — (labels only; emits no edges) | — |
289: 
290: ### 4.2 Routing
291: 
292: - Orthogonal elbows, **at most two bends** per path.
293: - Use a Q-bezier 8-px corner radius at every bend.
294: - Z-order: draw **all connectors before any node rectangle** (so node fills mask the line ends).
295: - Exactly one `marker-end` per `<path>` / `<line>`. Never both `marker-start` and `marker-end`.
296: - Labels: every `primary` and `secondary` connector gets a label (small mono, opaque paper-filled rect mask behind). `trigger` and `query` connectors are unlabelled.
297: 
298: ### 4.3 Crossings
299: 
300: - Avoid. Re-route via the chevron divider trunk (§5) before accepting a crossing.
301: - If unavoidable, the path drawn second carries a 6-px arc hop over the first.
302: 
303: ### 4.4 Component color override
304: 
305: A component may declare an optional `color: "#hex"` (CSS color string). The override **only** retints the component's container and content — connectors are never recolored. Edges keep their topology-driven style from §4.
306: 
307: **Where the color is applied** (given `C = color`):
308: 
309: | Element | Light mode | Dark mode |
310: |---|---|---|
311: | Container fill (`rect` body) | `rgba(C, 0.06)` | `rgba(C, 0.10)` |
312: | Container stroke | `rgba(C, 0.35)` (`stroke-width=1` for nodes, `0.8` for bars) | `rgba(C, 0.45)` |
313: | Role badge stroke (nodes) | `rgba(C, 0.40)` | `rgba(C, 0.55)` |
314: | Role badge text (nodes) | `rgba(C, 0.85)` | `rgba(C, 1.0)` |
315: | Icon fill / stroke | `C` | lighten `C` by ~15% (or use `C` if already light) |
316: | Name text | `C` | lighten `C` |
317: | Subtitle text | **unchanged** (`muted`) | **unchanged** (`muted`) |
318: | Connectors touching this component | **unchanged** (still topology-driven) | **unchanged** |
319: 
320: The subtitle stays muted because it's parenthetical metadata — only the primary identity (name + icon + border) carries the color signal.
321: 
322: **Rules**:
323: 
324: - **Never on the focal node.** The focal node is already colored with the accent (§3.7). A `color` on the focal node is ignored — accent wins.
325: - **Never on source nodes.** Sources live outside the cluster and stay neutral.
326: - **Cap at 2 custom-colored components** per diagram (in addition to the focal). Three or more colored things erases the signal — the same reason SKILL.md §3 limits accent to 1–2 elements.
327: - **No color on connectors.** If you find yourself wanting a colored edge, the right move is to pick a different `style` from §4, not to override.
328: 
329: **Semantic uses** (recommended):
330: - `#b85450` (rust-red) — Security / Identity (Keycloak, Vault)
331: - `#5a7d9a` (slate-blue) — Observability (Prometheus, Datadog)
332: - `#7a8c47` (olive-green) — Governance / Lineage (OpenMetadata)
333: - `#8c6d3f` (warm-brown) — Backup / DR
334: 
335: Stick to these unless the user's brand demands otherwise. Random hex per component is exactly the failure mode this skill avoids.
336: 
337: ---
338: 
339: ## 5. BLOCK BRANCHING RULES (FAN-OUT)
340: 
341: The single biggest reproducibility hazard. Fix these rules and the diagram becomes predictable.
342: 
343: ### 5.1 Source fan-out (one source → N components)
344: 
345: ```
346: exit_x   = source.right
347: trunk_x  = cluster_x - 8                     # 4-px gutter before cluster border
348: ```
349: 
350: Path per target: `M exit_x,source_cy → H trunk_x → V target_cy → H target.left`. Use Q-bezier corners.
351: 
352: ### 5.2 Component fan-out (one component → N components)
353: 
354: ```
355: exit_x   = node.right
356: trunk_x  = x_boundaries[index(source.chevron) + 1] + 4   # 4 px past the chevron divider
357: ```
358: 
359: Path per target: `M exit_x,source_cy → H trunk_x → V target_cy → H target.left`.
360: 
361: ### 5.3 Fan-out cap
362: 
363: **Max 3 outgoing edges per node.** Above 3, introduce a hub (usually the `focal` node). The chevron banner is the legend; if a node is fanning out to four downstream targets, it's secretly the hub — make it explicit.
364: 
365: ### 5.4 Bar drops (Airflow → N nodes)
366: 
367: ```
368: drop_x(target) = target.cx
369: drop_y_start   = bar.bottom
370: drop_y_end     = target.top
371: ```
372: 
373: Straight vertical line, `style: trigger`. One per target. No bends — bar drops never elbow.
374: 
375: ### 5.5 Source vertical staggering
376: 
377: When multiple sources connect to the same single target (e.g. four sources → NiFi), stagger their entry y on the target:
378: 
379: ```
380: entry_y(k) = target.top + 8 + k * (target_h - 16) / (N - 1)   # k = 0..N-1, evenly spaced
381: ```
382: 
383: This avoids overlapping arrowheads at the target's left edge.
384: 
385: ---
386: 
387: ## 6. VERTICAL CHEVRONS — SEMANTICS
388: 
389: Reserved names `Orchestration`, `Security`, `Observability`, `Governance`, `Backup` always render in the right strip (§3.9). Any chevron with `vertical: true` is treated as a reserved-style vertical regardless of name. The rules:
390: 
391: - **Pairing rule (mandatory, 1:1):** every vertical chevron pairs with exactly one cross-spanning component, and every cross-spanning component pairs with exactly one vertical chevron. The two component kinds that pair:
392:   - `kind: bar` — lives inside the cluster (top row). Conventionally paired with `Orchestration`.
393:   - `kind: cross-cutting` — lives below the cluster, one row per component. Paired with `Security`, `Observability`, `Governance`, etc.
394: 
395:   If the inputs declare a vertical chevron without a paired component (or vice versa), halt and ask the user — the diagram is incomplete.
396: 
397: - **Count constraint:** `len(verticals) == len(bars) + len(crosscuts)`. The right strip is split evenly among all verticals (§3.9), so visual alignment between a chevron and its bar/row is approximate — the *label* is what matters, not the y-pixel match.
398: 
399: - **Ordering convention:** declare verticals top-down in the order: bar-paired first (Orchestration), then crosscut-paired in the same order the crosscuts appear below the cluster. This keeps the visual reading order consistent.
400: 
401: - **No edges:** vertical chevrons emit no connectors themselves. They are *labels for a column of cross-cutting concern*.
402: 
403: - **No node placement:** no `kind: node` may be assigned to a vertical chevron. Nodes always belong to a horizontal phase.
404: 
405: - **Right strip presence:** if any vertical chevron exists, the right strip is reserved (`effective_w = 964`) and **all** horizontal chevron widths and cluster geometry shrink accordingly. Do not draw a vertical chevron on top of the cluster.
406: 
407: The visual contract: the vertical chevron's column visually "owns" the bar/cross-cutting row at its approximate y-band. Orchestration (top of strip) ↔ Airflow bar (top of cluster). Security ↔ Identity bar. Observability ↔ monitoring bar (below identity). And so on.
408: 
409: ---
410: 
411: ## 7. DARK MODE
412: 
413: When `dark: true`, swap these tokens:
414: 
415: | Token | Light | Dark |
416: |---|---|---|
417: | Page paper | `#f5f5f5` | `#1c1f2e` |
418: | Ink | `#2d3142` | `#f5f5f5` |
419: | Muted text | `#4f5d75` | `rgba(245,245,245,0.65)` |
420: | Chevron dark fill | `#2d3142` | `#3d4460` |
421: | Chevron light fill | `#3d4460` | `#4a5270` |
422: | Chevron label | `#f5f5f5` | `#f5f5f5` (unchanged) |
423: | Dashed border | `rgba(45,49,66,0.20)` | `rgba(245,245,245,0.22)` |
424: | Cluster border | `rgba(45,49,66,0.18)` | `rgba(245,245,245,0.18)` |
425: | Node fill | white | `rgba(245,245,245,0.06)` |
426: | Node stroke | `rgba(45,49,66,0.25)` | `rgba(245,245,245,0.20)` |
427: | Focal fill | `rgba(235,108,54,0.08)` | `rgba(240,138,89,0.12)` |
428: | Focal stroke | `#eb6c36` | `#f08a59` |
429: | Accent connector | `#eb6c36` | `#f08a59` |
430: | Dot pattern | `rgba(45,49,66,0.10)` | `rgba(245,245,245,0.10)` |
431: 
432: ---
433: 
434: ## 8. REPRODUCIBILITY CHECKLIST (THE TASTE GATE)
435: 
436: Before emitting SVG, verify **every** item. If any fails, fix it — don't ship.
437: 
438: 1. Every cluster `node.cx` equals its chevron's `cx` (§3.2 + §3.7). This is what makes the chevron banner a real legend.
439: 2. Every chevron `width` is a multiple of 4 and ≥ 120.
440: 3. The reserved right strip (28 px) exists **iff** any vertical chevron is declared. If yes, `effective_w = 972`; if no, `effective_w = 1000`.
441: 4. Exactly **one** `focal` node. If `focal` is unset in inputs, default to the first `kind: node` under chevron "Storage".
442: 5. Every edge whose endpoint is the focal node uses `style: primary` (accent stroke + `arrow-accent` marker).
443: 6. Every edge originating from a `kind: bar` component uses `style: trigger` (dashed + `arrow-sm`).
444: 7. The cross-cutting bar (if any) emits **no** edges.
445: 8. No node has > 3 outgoing edges, or if it does, it is the declared `focal` / hub.
446: 9. All `<path>` and `<line>` connectors are emitted **before** any node `<rect>` (z-order).
447: 10. Each vertical chevron pairs **1:1** with exactly one `bar` or `cross-cutting` component (§6 pairing rule). `len(verticals) == len(bars) + len(crosscuts)`.
448: 11. `viewBox_h = max(540, strip_y_bot + 112)` — grow the canvas when multiple crosscuts are declared so the legend still fits.
449: 12. Custom component colors (§4.4) apply only to container + icon + name; connectors stay topology-driven. Cap at 2 custom-colored components in addition to the focal.
450: 11. The diagram passes SKILL.md §6 (4-px grid; ≤ 2 accent elements; mono only for technical content; hairlines; no shadows; no `rounded-2xl`).
451: 
452: ---
453: 
454: ## 9. ANTI-PATTERNS
455: 
456: - Chevron banner omitted — it's the key that maps visual columns to functional phases.
457: - Node x-center off-chevron (§8 #1) — breaks the "banner-as-legend" contract.
458: - Vertical chevron drawn on the cluster (overlay) instead of in a reserved right strip.
459: - More than one focal node — MinIO/S3 (or whichever storage hub) is *the* focal point.
460: - External zone with solid border — dashed border is the signal that these components are outside the cluster.
461: - Identity bar inside the cluster boundary — it applies to all components and must span the full canvas width.
462: - Vertical chevron without a paired bar/cross-cutting component — see §6 pairing rule.
463: - Bar-component edges drawn solid — orchestration triggers must be dashed.
464: - Source fanning out to >3 components without a hub.
465: 
466: ---
467: 
468: ## 10. EXAMPLES
469: 
470: - `assets/diagrams/high-level.html` — horizontal-only, 5 phases, light skin.
471: - `assets/diagrams/high-level-dark.html` — same, dark skin.
472: - `assets/diagrams/high-level-full.html` — same, editorial-card frame.
473: - `assets/diagrams/high-level-vertical.html` — adds vertical Orchestration + Security chevrons, Airflow bar, Keycloak cross-cutting. **Reference render of the full parametric pattern.**
474: - `assets/diagrams/high-level-vertical-dark.html` — vertical pattern, dark skin.
475: - `assets/diagrams/high-level-vertical-full.html` — vertical pattern, editorial-card frame.
