16: # High-Level
17: 
18: ## 1. OVERVIEW
19: 
20: **Best for:** end-to-end data stack overviews — ingestion → storage → query → analytics → visualization — deployed on a container orchestrator (Kubernetes, ECS, Nomad). Combines a phase chevron banner, deployment boundary, orchestration bar, identity footer, and (optionally) a right-side vertical chevron strip for cross-cutting concerns (Orchestration, Security, Observability).
21: 
22: This type is **parametric**. The diagram is fully determined by a small list of inputs (chevrons, sources, components, connections). The formulas below tell you exactly where every shape lands given those inputs — two generations from the same inputs must produce visually identical SVG.
23: 
24: ---
25: 
26: ## 2. INPUTS — THE PARAMETER CONTRACT
27: 
28: Before drawing, collect these from the user (or accept them as a YAML/JSON block). Everything in this reference is derived from these inputs. Don't invent geometry on the fly.
29: 
30: ```yaml
31: chevrons:                       # ordered left → right; reserved names auto-promote to vertical
32:   - { name: "Data sources",         columns: 1 }
33:   - { name: "Ingestion",            columns: 1 }
34:   - { name: "Storage",              columns: 1 }
35:   - { name: "Transformation",       columns: 1 }
36:   - { name: "Visualization",        columns: 1 }
37:   - { name: "Orchestration",        vertical: true }                     # reserved → pairs with the bar
38:   - { name: "Security",             vertical: true, color: "#b85450" }   # tinted to match the Identity bar below
39:   - { name: "Observability",        vertical: true }                     # reserved → pairs with crosscut #2
40: 
41: sources:                        # external; rendered in the dashed zone on the left
42:   - { name: "PostgreSQL", type: "db",     connects_to: ["NiFi"] }
43:   - { name: "SFTP drop",  type: "ftp",    connects_to: ["NiFi"] }
44:   - { name: "Web forms",  type: "web",    connects_to: ["NiFi"] }
45:   - { name: "Legacy",     type: "legacy", connects_to: ["NiFi"] }
46: 
47: components:                     # inside the cluster, plus bars and cross-cutting rows
48:   - { name: "NiFi",       chevron: "Ingestion",      kind: node,          icon: nifi,     role: "COLL"  }
49:   - { name: "MinIO",      chevron: "Storage",        kind: node,          icon: minio,    role: "STORE", focal: true }
50:   - { name: "Trino",      chevron: "Storage",        kind: node,          icon: trino,    role: "VIRT"  }
51:   - { name: "Notebooks",  chevron: "Transformation", kind: node,          icon: jupyter,  role: "ANLZ"  }
52:   - { name: "Superset",   chevron: "Visualization",  kind: node,          icon: superset, role: "DASH" }

88: ## 3. LAYOUT FORMULAS — DETERMINISTIC GEOMETRY
89: 
90: Every coordinate below is derived from the inputs. **No hardcoded numbers in examples that aren't justified here.**
91: 
92: ### 3.1 Canvas
93: 
94: ```
95: has_vertical       = any(c.vertical or c.name in reserved_names for c in chevrons)
96: right_strip_w      = 28  if has_vertical else 0
97: strip_margin       = 8   if has_vertical else 0   # gap between body and right strip
98: effective_w        = 1000 - right_strip_w - strip_margin     # 1000 or 964
99: 
100: n_cross            = count of components with kind == "cross-cutting"
101: strip_y_bot        = max(428, 388 + n_cross * 44 - 4)        # extends to last crosscut row
102: viewBox_h          = max(540, strip_y_bot + 112)             # 112 reserved for legend
103: viewBox            = f"0 0 1000 {viewBox_h}"
104: ```
105: 
106: Every horizontal element (chevron banner, cluster, orchestration bar, identity / cross-cutting bars) ends at `effective_w`. The right strip sits at `x = 1000 - right_strip_w` (= 972). The 8-px band between them is visual breathing room — never put content there.
107: 
108: `viewBox_h` grows when more than one cross-cutting bar is declared: 1 crosscut → 540, 2 → 600 (or 584 if you want it tight; the rule rounds to the next multiple of 20 for clean grids).

110: ### 3.2 Horizontal chevron banner
111: 
112: ```
113: y_banner           = 4
114: h_banner           = 28
115: horizontals        = [c for c in chevrons if not c.vertical and c.name not in reserved_names]
116: sum_columns        = sum(c.columns for c in horizontals)
117: base_unit          = floor_to_4(effective_w / sum_columns)        # multiple of 4
118: widths             = [max(120, base_unit * c.columns) for c in horizontals]
119: widths[-1]         += effective_w - sum(widths)                   # trailing absorbs remainder
120: x_boundaries       = cumulative_sum([0] + widths)                 # length sum_columns+1
121: chevron_cx(C)      = (x_boundaries[index(C)] + x_boundaries[index(C)+1]) / 2
122: ```

Use it to flag a phase that pairs with a custom-colored component (e.g., `Security` chevron in red when the Identity bar uses `color: "#b85450"`). Rules:

258: ## 4. CONNECTOR RULES (MANDATORY)
259: 
260: These are non-negotiable. Pick the style **automatically** from the topology — do not let the user override style on focal-touching or bar-originating edges.
261: 
262: | `style` | Stroke | Width | Dash | Marker | When required |
263: |---|---|---|---|---|---|
264: | `primary` | `#eb6c36` | 1.2 | — | `arrow-accent` | Every edge whose endpoint is the `focal` node. |
265: | `secondary` | `#4f5d75` | 1.0 | — | `arrow` | Default for source→component and component→component when neither endpoint is focal. |
266: | `trigger` | `#4f5d75` | 1.0 | `4,3` | `arrow-sm` | Every edge originating from a `kind: bar` component. |
267: | `query` | `rgba(45,49,66,0.30)` | 1.0 | `4,3` | `arrow` | Read-back edges (e.g., focal ↔ Trino). |
268: 
269: **Defs block** (required, exactly these four markers):
270: 
271: ```svg
272: <defs>
273:   <marker id="arrow"        markerWidth="8" markerHeight="6" refX="7" refY="3"   orient="auto"><polygon points="0 0, 8 3, 0 6" fill="#4f5d75"/></marker>
274:   <marker id="arrow-accent" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="6" refX="7" refY="3"   orient="auto"><polygon points="0 0, 8 3, 0 6" fill="#eb6c36"/></marker>
275:   <marker id="arrow-sm"     markerWidth="6" markerHeight="5" refX="5" refY="2.5" orient="auto"><polygon points="0 0, 6 2.5, 0 5" fill="#4f5d75"/></marker>
276:   <marker id="arrow-dim"    markerWidth="8" markerHeight="6" refX="7" refY="3"   orient="auto"><polygon points="0 0, 8 3, 0 6" fill="rgba(45,49,66,0.45)"/></marker>
277: </defs>
278: ```
279: 
280: ### 4.1 Exit / entry sides (non-negotiable)
281: 
282: | Edge kind | Exit side of source | Entry side of target |
283: |---|---|---|
284: | Source → cluster node | **right** of source node | **left** of target |
285: | Component → component (within cluster) | **right** | **left** |
286: | Bar component → node | **bottom** of bar | **top** of node |
287: | Cross-cutting bar | — (emits no edges) | — |
288: | Vertical chevron | — (labels only; emits no edges) | — |
289: 
290: ### 4.2 Routing
291: 
292: - Orthogonal elbows, **at most two bends** per path.
293: - Use a Q-bezier 8-px corner radius at every bend.
294: - Z-order: draw **all connectors before any node rectangle** (so node fills mask the line ends).
295: - Exactly one `marker-end` per `<path>` / `<line>`. Never both `marker-start` and `marker-end`.
296: - Labels: every `primary` and `secondary` connector gets a label (small mono, opaque paper-filled rect mask behind). `trigger` and `query` connectors are unlabelled.
297: 
298: ### 4.3 Crossings
299: 
300: - Avoid. Re-route via the chevron divider trunk (§5) before accepting a crossing.
301: - If unavoidable, the path drawn second carries a 6-px arc hop over the first.
302: 
303: ### 4.4 Component color override
304: 
305: A component may declare an optional `color: "#hex"` (CSS color string). The override **only** retints the component's container and content — connectors are never recolored. Edges keep their topology-driven style from §4.
306: 
307: **Where the color is applied** (given `C = color`):
308: 
309: | Element | Light mode | Dark mode |
310: |---|---|---|
311: | Container fill (`rect` body) | `rgba(C, 0.06)` | `rgba(C, 0.10)` |
312: | Container stroke | `rgba(C, 0.35)` (`stroke-width=1` for nodes, `0.8` for bars) | `rgba(C, 0.45)` |
313: | Role badge stroke (nodes) | `rgba(C, 0.40)` | `rgba(C, 0.55)` |
314: | Role badge text (nodes) | `rgba(C, 0.85)` | `rgba(C, 1.0)` |
315: | Icon fill / stroke | `C` | lighten `C` by ~15% (or use `C` if already light) |
316: | Name text | `C` | lighten `C` |
317: | Subtitle text | **unchanged** (`muted`) | **unchanged** (`muted`) |
318: | Connectors touching this component | **unchanged** (still topology-driven) | **unchanged** |
319: 
320: The subtitle stays muted because it's parenthetical metadata — only the primary identity (name + icon + border) carries the color signal.
321: 
322: **Rules**:
323: 
324: - **Never on the focal node.** The focal node is already colored with the accent (§3.7). A `color` on the focal node is ignored — accent wins.
325: - **Never on source nodes.** Sources live outside the cluster and stay neutral.
326: - **Cap at 2 custom-colored components** per diagram (in addition to the focal). Three or more colored things erases the signal — the same reason SKILL.md §3 limits accent to 1–2 elements.
327: - **No color on connectors.** If you find yourself wanting a colored edge, the right move is to pick a different `style` from §4, not to override.
328: 
329: **Semantic uses** (recommended):
330: - `#b85450` (rust-red) — Security / Identity (Keycloak, Vault)
331: - `#5a7d9a` (slate-blue) — Observability (Prometheus, Datadog)
332: - `#7a8c47` (olive-green) — Governance / Lineage (OpenMetadata)
333: - `#8c6d3f` (warm-brown) — Backup / DR
334: 
335: Stick to these unless the user's brand demands otherwise. Random hex per component is exactly the failure mode this skill avoids.

339: ## 5. BLOCK BRANCHING RULES (FAN-OUT)
340: 
341: The single biggest reproducibility hazard. Fix these rules and the diagram becomes predictable.
342: 
343: ### 5.1 Source fan-out (one source → N components)
344: 
345: ```
346: exit_x   = source.right
347: trunk_x  = cluster_x - 8                     # 4-px gutter before cluster border
348: ```
349: 
350: Path per target: `M exit_x,source_cy → H trunk_x → V target_cy → H target.left`. Use Q-bezier corners.
351: 
352: ### 5.2 Component fan-out (one component → N components)
353: 
354: ```
355: exit_x   = node.right
356: trunk_x  = x_boundaries[index(source.chevron) + 1] + 4   # 4 px past the chevron divider
357: ```
358: 
359: Path per target: `M exit_x,source_cy → H trunk_x → V target_cy → H target.left`.
360: 
361: ### 5.3 Fan-out cap
362: 
363: **Max 3 outgoing edges per node.** Above 3, introduce a hub (usually the `focal` node). The chevron banner is the legend; if a node is fanning out to four downstream targets, it's secretly the hub — make it explicit.
364: 
365: ### 5.4 Bar drops (Airflow → N nodes)
366: 
367: ```
368: drop_x(target) = target.cx
369: drop_y_start   = bar.bottom
370: drop_y_end     = target.top
371: ```
372: 
373: Straight vertical line, `style: trigger`. One per target. No bends — bar drops never elbow.
374: 
375: ### 5.5 Source vertical staggering
376: 
377: When multiple sources connect to the same single target (e.g. four sources → NiFi), stagger their entry y on the target:
378: 
379: ```
380: entry_y(k) = target.top + 8 + k * (target_h - 16) / (N - 1)   # k = 0..N-1, evenly spaced
381: ```
382: 
383: This avoids overlapping arrowheads at the target's left edge.

387: ## 6. VERTICAL CHEVRONS — SEMANTICS
388: 
389: Reserved names `Orchestration`, `Security`, `Observability`, `Governance`, `Backup` always render in the right strip (§3.9). Any chevron with `vertical: true` is treated as a reserved-style vertical regardless of name. The rules:
390: 
391: - **Pairing rule (mandatory, 1:1):** every vertical chevron pairs with exactly one cross-spanning component, and every cross-spanning component pairs with exactly one vertical chevron. The two component kinds that pair:
392:   - `kind: bar` — lives inside the cluster (top row). Conventionally paired with `Orchestration`.
393:   - `kind: cross-cutting` — lives below the cluster, one row per component. Paired with `Security`, `Observability`, `Governance`, etc.
394: 
395:   If the inputs declare a vertical chevron without a paired component (or vice versa), halt and ask the user — the diagram is incomplete.
396: 
397: - **Count constraint:** `len(verticals) == len(bars) + len(crosscuts)`. The right strip is split evenly among all verticals (§3.9), so visual alignment between a chevron and its bar/row is approximate — the *label* is what matters, not the y-pixel match.
398: 
399: - **Ordering convention:** declare verticals top-down in the order: bar-paired first (Orchestration), then crosscut-paired in the same order the crosscuts appear below the cluster. This keeps the visual reading order consistent.
400: 
401: - **No edges:** vertical chevrons emit no connectors themselves. They are *labels for a column of cross-cutting concern*.
402: 
403: - **No node placement:** no `kind: node` may be assigned to a vertical chevron. Nodes always belong to a horizontal phase.
404: 
405: - **Right strip presence:** if any vertical chevron exists, the right strip is reserved (`effective_w = 964`) and **all** horizontal chevron widths and cluster geometry shrink accordingly. Do not draw a vertical chevron on top of the cluster.
406: 
407: The visual contract: the vertical chevron's column visually "owns" the bar/cross-cutting row at its approximate y-band. Orchestration (top of strip) ↔ Airflow bar (top of cluster). Security ↔ Identity bar. Observability ↔ monitoring bar (below identity). And so on.

434: ## 8. REPRODUCIBILITY CHECKLIST (THE TASTE GATE)
435: 
436: Before emitting SVG, verify **every** item. If any fails, fix it — don't ship.
437:

223: ## 4. CONNECTOR RULES (MANDATORY)

225: ### 4.1 Path shape — rounded right-angle Q-bezier, r = 8
226: 
227: Reused verbatim from `type-process.md` §4.1. No diagonals — ever.
228: 
229: ```svg
230: <!-- Same zone, adjacent component (same vertical column): single vertical line -->
231: <line x1="{src_cx}" y1="{src_bot}" x2="{dst_cx}" y2="{dst_top}"
232:       stroke="…" stroke-width="…" marker-end="…"/>
233: 
234: <!-- Cross-zone or cross-row: exit right → H → Q-bend → V → enter top (or bottom) -->
235: <path d="M {src_right},{src_cy}  H {dst_cx - 8}  Q {dst_cx},{src_cy} {dst_cx},{src_cy ± 8}  V {dst_top_or_bottom}"
236:       fill="none" stroke="…" stroke-width="…" marker-end="…"/>
237: ```
238: 
239: - Use `{src_cy + 8}` and `V {dst_top}` when destination lies BELOW source.
240: - Use `{src_cy − 8}` and `V {dst_bottom}` when destination lies ABOVE source.
241: 
242: ### 4.2 Exit / entry sides (configurable; defaults below)
243: 
244: | Topology | Default exit side of source | Default entry side of destination |
245: | --- | --- | --- |
246: | Same zone, dst below | bottom | top |
247: | Same zone, dst above | top | bottom |
248: | Cross-zone, horizontal flow | right | top (or bottom, whichever is closer to src_cy) |
249: | Vertical-orientation diagram | bottom | top |
250: 
251: A connector can override via `connectors[k].from_side` / `connectors[k].to_side` (`top | right | bottom | left`). **Backward references** (right→left in horizontal orientation, up in vertical orientation) are permitted only when at least one endpoint has `kind: external`, and must be `dashed: true`.
252: 
253: ### 4.3 Markers MUST touch the destination rectangle
254: 
255: The path's last command ends at the destination's rectangle edge (`V {dst_top}` or `H {dst_left}`), **not** at the centroid. After applying `refX=7` on the marker, the triangle sits flush against the border. Stopping the line short of the edge — or sending it to the centroid and burying the arrowhead inside the rect — is a hard fail.
256: 
257: ### 4.4 Style → stroke + marker
258: 
259: | `style` | Stroke color | Stroke width | Marker |
260: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
261: | `neutral` | `muted` | 1.0 | `url(#arrow)` |
262: | `link` | `link` | 1.2 | `url(#arrow-link)` |
263: | `accent` | `accent` | 1.4 | `url(#arrow-accent)` |
264: 
265: Add `stroke-dasharray="4 3"` when `dashed: true`.
266: 
267: **Defs block** (always emit all three):
268: 
269: ```svg
270: <defs>
271:   <marker id="arrow"        markerWidth="8" markerHeight="6" refX="7" refY="3" orient="auto"><polygon points="0 0, 8 3, 0 6" fill="{muted}"/></marker>
272:   <marker id="arrow-link"   markerWidth="8" markerHeight="6" refX="7" refY="3" orient="auto"><polygon points="0 0, 8 3, 0 6" fill="{link}"/></marker>
273:   <marker id="arrow-accent" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="6" refX="7" refY="3" orient="auto"><polygon points="0 0, 8 3, 0 6" fill="{accent}"/></marker>
274: </defs>
275: ```
276: 
277: ### 4.5 Connector label = inline icon + text, placed at the START of the connector with a perpendicular margin
278: 
279: The label sits **near the source end** of the connector (not at the mid-segment) and is **offset perpendicular to the line** so it never overlaps the stroke. Icon (when `icon:` is set) sits inside the label's paper-fill mask, to the left of the text.
280: 
281: ```svg
282: <g transform="translate({label_cx}, {label_cy})">
283:   <rect x="-{w/2}" y="-9" width="{w}" height="18" rx="3" fill="{paper}" stroke="none"/>
284:   <use href="#icon-{icon}" x="-{w/2 + 4}" y="-6" width="12" height="12" color="{stroke_color}"/>     <!-- if icon set -->
285:   <text x="{icon ? (-(w/2) + 22) : 0}" y="3" text-anchor="{icon ? 'start' : 'middle'}"
286:         font-family="{arrow-label}" font-size="9" font-weight="600"
287:         letter-spacing="0.08em" fill="{stroke_color}">{label}</text>
288: </g>
289: ```
290: 
291: **Placement formulas** (label box is 18px tall × `w` wide; centered on `{label_cx, label_cy}`):
292: 
293: | Segment exiting source | `label_cx` | `label_cy` | Effect |
294: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
295: | Horizontal (right exit) | `src_right + 6 + w/2` | `src_cy − 14` | Label sits 6 px past the source, 5 px above the line |
296: | Horizontal (left exit, backward) | `src_left − 6 − w/2` | `src_cy − 14` | Label sits 6 px before the source, 5 px above the line |
297: | Vertical (bottom exit) | `src_cx + 6 + w/2` | `src_bot + 14` | Label sits 6 px right of the line, 5 px below the source edge |
298: | Vertical (top exit, backward) | `src_cx + 6 + w/2` | `src_top − 14` | Label sits 6 px right of the line, 5 px above the source edge |
299: 
300: For cross-zone H+Q+V routes the label binds to the **horizontal** segment, since that segment is anchored at the source. Place the label early on that horizontal run — never on the Q-bend or the vertical tail.
301: 
302: - `w = text_w + (icon ? 30 : 12)` — auto-fit.
303: - Mask `fill` resolves to `paper` in light mode and `ink` in dark mode. The mask is kept as a safety pad — even though the label no longer sits on the line, it can graze zone backgrounds and component fills, and the mask preserves contrast.
304: - `stroke_color` follows §4.4 (text + icon inherit the connector's accent / link / neutral color).
305: 
306: ### 4.6 Z-order
307: 
308: All connectors (paths + lines + labels) emit BEFORE any component rect, so node fills mask the line ends. The connector label is the exception — it draws AFTER its line so the mask sits on top.

312: ## 5. COMPONENT COLOR OVERRIDE (PER-COMPONENT `color: "#hex"`)
313: 
314: Per-component, same shape as every other parametric type in this skill.
315: 
316: | Element | Light | Dark |
317: | --- | --- | --- |
318: | Container fill | `rgba(C, 0.06)` | `rgba(C_light, 0.10)` |
319: | Container stroke | `rgba(C, 0.45)` (width 1) | `rgba(C_light, 0.55)` |
320: | Component name text | `C` | `C_light` |
321: | Icon glyph | inherits ink via `currentColor` (unchanged) | inherits ink (unchanged) |
322: | Sub-label | muted (unchanged) | muted (unchanged) |
323: | Connectors touching this component | **unchanged** — topology-driven | **unchanged** |
324: 
325: `C_light` = the same hex lightened ~15 % for dark-mode contrast (e.g., `#7a8c47` → `#9aac67`, `#b85450` → `#d97a78`).
326: 
327: **Rules:**
328: - **Never on focal components.** `kind: focal` always renders accent; `color` is silently ignored.
329: - **Never on connectors.** Connector style is topology-driven; if you want a colored edge, pick `style: accent` / `link` / `neutral`, not a component color.
330: - **Cap: ≤ 3 custom-colored components per diagram** (in addition to focal components). Above 3 the visual signal fragments.
331: 
332: **Recommended cross-type palette** (same as `type-medallion.md` / `type-process.md` / `type-dp-integration.md` / `type-dp-security-matrix.md`):
333: 
334: - `#b85450` rust-red — security / governance / pain-point that isn't focal
335: - `#5a7d9a` slate-blue — observability / quality / monitoring gate
336: - `#7a8c47` olive-green — survivor system (the one tool the new platform keeps)
337: - `#c9a23a` warm yellow — sandbox / dev / scratch
338: - `#8c6d3f` warm-brown — archive / cold / DR

342: ## 6. FOCAL RULE
343: 
344: - `kind: focal` components: **≤ 2 per diagram** (zero is also valid for diagrams without a single dominant pain-point).
345: - Auto-styling: accent stroke 1.4, accent-tinted fill 7 %, ink-bold `node-name`, accent line-1 `sublabel`.
346: - Any connector with a focal endpoint automatically renders in `style: accent`; the YAML `style:` is ignored.
347: - Custom `color: "#hex"` on a focal component is silently ignored — accent always wins.
348: 
349: If your diagram needs more than 2 focal components, you've collapsed two narratives. Split: one "collection pain-points" diagram + one "dissemination pain-points" diagram.

353: ## 7. DARK MODE
354: 
355: | Role | Light | Dark |
356: | --- | --- | --- |
357: | paper | `paper` | `ink` |
358: | ink | `ink` | `paper` |
359: | muted | `muted` | `muted` |
360: | accent | `accent` | `accent` |
361: | link | `link` | `link` |
362: | zone background | `ink @ 0.02` | `paper @ 0.04` |
363: | zone border | `ink @ 0.10` | `paper @ 0.14` |
364: | standard component fill | `#FFFFFF` | `paper @ 0.04` |
365: | standard component stroke | `ink` | `paper @ 0.32` |
366: | focal fill | `accent @ 0.07` | `accent @ 0.12` |
367: | focal stroke | `accent` | `accent` |
368: | external stroke | `muted` (dashed) | `muted` (dashed) |
369: | footer fill | `ink @ 0.03` | `paper @ 0.05` |
370: | footer stroke | `ink @ 0.18` | `paper @ 0.20` |
371: | label mask fill | `paper` | `ink` |
372: | custom-color components | `C` | `C_light` (≈ +15 %) |
373: 
374: ---
375: 
376: ## 8. REPRODUCIBILITY CHECKLIST (TASTE GATE)
377: 
378: Before emitting SVG, verify **every** item:
379: 
380: 1. Eyebrow + title + subtitle present at canonical y-positions (24 / 36 / 52); body padding 32 px.
381: 2. 2..4 zones; each has its uppercase label at the top-left of its zone box, on a paper-masked break in the border.
382: 3. Every component has `id`, `name`. `sub`, `icon`, `kind`, `color` are optional.
383: 4. ≤ 2 components with `kind: focal`; focal styling auto-applied (accent fill 7 %, accent stroke 1.4, italic line-1 sub).
384: 5. Every connector exits the right (or bottom) of source and enters the top (or left) of destination; rounded right-angle Q-bezier `r=8` at every bend; marker triangle visibly touches the destination rectangle edge.
385: 6. Connector labels sit at the **start** of the connector (not mid-segment) and are offset **perpendicular** to the line (5 px gap above for horizontal segments, 6 px gap to the right for vertical segments) — never overlapping the stroke. Paper-fill mask kept behind text; icon (when `icon:` is set) sits left of text inside the same mask.
386: 7. ≤ 3 custom-colored components; none on focal.
387: 8. ≤ 3 footer bars; each spans `viewBox_w − 2*left_pad`; no connectors emerge from any footer.
388: 9. Legend at bottom: hairline separator + one swatch per style actually used.
389: 10. `arrow-label` for connector labels, `eyebrow` for the page eyebrow and zone labels, `title` for the page title, `node-name` for the subtitle and component names, and `sublabel` for technical sub-labels.
390: 11. Markers `#arrow` / `#arrow-link` / `#arrow-accent` defined once in `<defs>`; no inline marker definitions.
391: 12. Dark variant: resolve every semantic token through its dark-mode value; custom colors are lightened ~15 %.
392: 
393: ---
394: 
395: ## 9. ANTI-PATTERNS
396: 
397: - **Diagonal arrows.** The NatStat replication has one (analyst → LegacyPortal). The new type forbids it — always rounded right-angle Q-bezier.
398: - **Marker not touching the target.** Path ends at the centroid or stops short of the border.
399: - **Inline `text` connector labels without a mask rect.** The connector line can bleed through the text and it becomes unreadable.
400: - **Labels sitting on top of the connector line, mid-segment.** Labels belong at the *start* of the connector with a perpendicular margin (see §4.5) — burying them in the middle of the line hides the source-to-destination direction and forces the reader's eye to fight the mask.
401: - **Tiny text badges as icons.** The source uses 7-px `DB` / `APP` / `EXT` badges; this type uses real 24-px catalog icons. Text badges are only acceptable as the label text, not as the component "icon."
402: - **Custom color on a focal component.** Focal always wins; user-set `color` silently ignored on `kind: focal`.
403: - **Footer bar wired to one component.** Footer = cross-cutting layer-wide concern; a connector from a footer to a specific component is a category error (use `type-dp-integration.md`'s AUTH-line pattern only when the footer service truly authenticates *all* components, and even then the line lands at the zone bottom edge, not at a specific tool).
404: - **> 16 total components or > 5 per zone.** Density cap; split into two diagrams.
405: - **Mixing orientations within one diagram.** Pick one — `horizontal` or `vertical` — and apply it to every zone.
406: - **Using `kind: focal` to flag every painful thing.** Focal exists for ≤ 2 narrative pain-points; for "this is bad but not headline-bad", use `color: "#b85450"` rust-red instead.
407: 
408: ---
409: 
410: ## 10. EXAMPLES
411: 
412: - `assets/diagrams/it-state.html` — minimal light (NatStat canonical: 3 zones, 9 components, 8 connectors, 0 footer bars, SQL Server tinted olive). Gallery default.
413: - `assets/diagrams/it-state-dark.html` — same, dark skin.
414: - `assets/diagrams/it-state-full.html` — same, editorial-card frame with summary cards.
415: - `assets/diagrams/it-state-extended.html` — exercises §5 color override + footer bars: 2 footer bars (Identity Manager + Observability) below the zones, third custom color on Analyst Machines (slate-blue, data-quality concern).
416: - `assets/diagrams/it-state-extended-dark.html` — extended pattern, dark skin.
417: 
418: ---
419: 
420: ## 11. WORKED YAML — FULL INPUTS FOR `it-state.html`
421: 
422: The complete inputs that map to the shipped canonical example. Every coordinate in that SVG is derivable from §3 applied to these inputs.
423: 
424: ```yaml
425: title:    "Current IT Landscape"
426: subtitle: "Data pipeline before the platform"
427: eyebrow:  "NatStat · Before the platform"
428: 
429: orientation: horizontal
430: 
431: zones:
432:   - name: "COLLECTION"
433:     components:
434:       - { id: survey-solutions, name: "Survey Solutions", sub: "CAPI · PostgreSQL",          icon: postgres }
435:       - { id: aspnet,           name: "ASP.NET Apps",     sub: "migration · admin portals", icon: server   }
436:       - { id: civil-reg,        name: "Civil Registry",   sub: "external · CRVS data",      icon: database, kind: external }
437:   - name: "PROCESSING"
438:     components:
439:       - { id: shared-drive,  name: "Shared Drive",     sub: "No version control · Windows file share", icon: file,      kind: focal }
440:       - { id: analyst-mach,  name: "Analyst Machines", sub: "SPSS · SAS · Stata · Excel",              icon: desktop }
441:       - { id: sql-server,    name: "SQL Server",       sub: "on-premises · core RDBMS",                icon: sqlserver, color: "#7a8c47" }
442:   - name: "DISSEMINATION"
443:     components:
444:       - { id: legacy-portal,   name: "LegacyPortal",      sub: "manual bottleneck",     icon: cloud,    kind: focal }
445:       - { id: natstat-website, name: "NatStat Website",   sub: "public · static pages", icon: internet }
446:       - { id: ministry,        name: "Ministry Partners", sub: "~6 ministries",         icon: users,    kind: external }
447: 
448: connectors:
449:   - { from: survey-solutions, to: shared-drive,   label: "CSV",    icon: csv,   style: link }
450:   - { from: aspnet,           to: shared-drive,   label: "EMAIL",  icon: file,  style: link }
451:   - { from: civil-reg,        to: shared-drive,   label: "EXCEL",  icon: excel, style: link, dashed: true }
452:   - { from: shared-drive,     to: analyst-mach,   label: "COPY",                style: accent, dashed: true }
453:   - { from: analyst-mach,     to: sql-server,     label: "LOAD",                style: neutral }
454:   - { from: analyst-mach,     to: legacy-portal,   label: "EXCEL",  icon: excel, style: accent }
455:   - { from: legacy-portal,    to: natstat-website, label: "WEB",                 style: neutral }
456:   - { from: natstat-website,  to: ministry,        label: "CSV DL", icon: csv,   style: link, dashed: true }
457: 
458: dark: false
459: ```
460: 
461: ### 11.1 What this YAML proves
462: 
463: - `n_zones = 3`, components per zone `= [3, 3, 3]`, custom color count = 1 (SQL Server), focal count = 2 (Shared Drive, LegacyPortal), external count = 2 (Civil Registry, Ministry Partners).
464: - Zone widths in canonical: 256 / 360 / 272 ⇒ `viewBox_w = 16 + 256 + 20 + 360 + 20 + 272 + 16 = 960` ✓
465: - `viewBox_h = 52 + 360 + 40 + 24 = 500` (no footer bars) ✓
466: - Shared Drive (focal) at zone 2, row 0: `x = 340, y = 80, w = 264, h = 68` (focal stretches to 68 to fit 2-line sub) ✓
467: - LegacyPortal (focal) at zone 3, row 0: `x = 704, y = 80, w = 208, h = 60` ✓
468: - SQL Server (custom olive) at zone 2, row 2: container fill `rgba(122,140,71,0.06)`, stroke `rgba(122,140,71,0.45)`, name text `#7a8c47` ✓
469: - Connectors 4, 5 (within zone 2) and 7, 8 (within zone 3) are simple vertical `<line>` elements. Cross-zone connectors take rule-compliant routes (see SKILL.md §4 rules 14 & 15):
470:   - **All three Survey-side → Shared Drive connectors (C1 / C2 / C3) enter Shared Drive's LEFT edge.** A top-edge entry would push the marker body (7 px back along travel, given `refX = 7`) *inside* the destination box, where the box's paper-fill mask hides it — only a 1-pixel tip would peek above the stroke. Entering the left edge with a right-going path keeps the body outside the box and the arrow visible (~7 px shown to the left of the box edge). The three left-edge attach points are fanned at **y = 108 / 124 / 140** (16-px spacing, well above the 12 px rule 14 minimum).
471:   - **C1** (Survey → Shared Drive) source y matches landing y: single horizontal `M 252,108 H 340`. No bends needed.
472:   - **C2** (ASP.NET → Shared Drive) detours up through zone-2 background — vertical at `x = 316` (clear of Shared Drive's left edge at `x = 340`): `H 308 Q 316,196 316,188 V 132 Q 316,124 324,124 H 340`. Lands at `(340, 124)`.
473:   - **C3** (Civil Registry → Shared Drive) detours up through zone-2 background — vertical at `x = 332` (clear of Analyst Machines, which starts at `x = 340`): `H 324 Q 332,284 332,276 V 148 Q 332,140 340,140`. Lands at `(340, 140)` via a final Q-bend (no trailing H needed).
474:   - **C6** (Analyst Machines → LegacyPortal) cannot use a direct H+Q+V into LegacyPortal's left edge — Analyst Machines and LegacyPortal are in different rows, and the direct horizontal at `y = 268` would cross NatStat Website. It detours through the zone gap and **over** LegacyPortal: `H 654 Q 662,268 662,260 V 72 Q 662,64 670,64 H 800 Q 808,64 808,72 V 80` — vertical at `x = 662` (in zone gap), horizontal at `y = 64` (above LegacyPortal top), then down into LegacyPortal's top center. The path enters LegacyPortal from **above** going down, so the arrow body lives above the box (visible) and only the 1-px tip enters the box.
475: 
476: **Marker-visibility rule of thumb:** with the standard arrow marker (`markerWidth = 8`, `refX = 7`), the arrow body extends 7 px *backwards* along the path direction from the endpoint. For the arrow to remain visible, that 7-px tail must sit *outside* the destination box. Translation:
477: - Entering a **TOP edge going UP** (path direction up, box below) → body inside box, **only 1 px visible. Avoid this.**
478: - Entering a **TOP edge going DOWN** (path direction down, box below) → body above box, ~7 px visible. ✓
479: - Entering a **LEFT edge going RIGHT** → body to the left of box, ~7 px visible. ✓
480: - Entering a **RIGHT edge going LEFT** → body to the right of box, ~7 px visible. ✓
481: - Entering a **BOTTOM edge going DOWN** (box above) → body inside box, **only 1 px visible. Avoid this.**
482: - Entering a **BOTTOM edge going UP** (box above) → body below box, ~7 px visible. ✓
483: 
484: When the source row matches the destination row's y range (e.g., Survey at y=108 with Shared Drive at y=80–148), prefer **side-edge** entry — a single horizontal path with a fully visible arrow. When the source row is offset, detour through the destination's nearest zone background to enter a side edge rather than approaching a top/bottom edge from the wrong side.

486: The extended example (§10 line 4) demonstrates footer bars + a third custom color and proves `viewBox_h` grows correctly when `N_footer > 0`.

14: 
15: # IT current-state
16: 
17: ## 1. OVERVIEW
18: 
19: **Best for:** documenting the *before* picture of a modernization proposal — the legacy IT landscape grouped by phase or department (Collection → Processing → Dissemination, or Frontend / Backend / Storage, or Survey → Analysts → Reports), with pain-points flagged, file-based hand-offs labelled (CSV / Excel / Email / Copy), and pre-platform tooling visible. The companion to `type-dp-integration.md`: this type shows the gap that a data-platform proposal is going to close.
20: 
21: Use when stakeholders need to see the friction in the current setup — siloed scripts, manual file shuffles, missing version control, single-points-of-failure — and the path from those to a target platform topology.
22: 
23: This type is **parametric** — the inputs schema in §2 drives every coordinate via the formulas in §3. The rule shape mirrors `type-dp-integration.md` (zones + cross-cutting footer bars), `type-process.md` (rounded right-angle connectors), and `type-medallion.md` (per-element `color` override) so the focal rule, color override, dark mode, and reproducibility checklist read identically across types.
24: 
25: ---
26: 
27: ## 2. INPUTS — THE PARAMETER CONTRACT
28: 
29: ```yaml
30: title:    "Current IT Landscape"
31: subtitle: "Data pipeline before the platform"
32: eyebrow:  "NatStat · Before the platform"
33: 
34: orientation: horizontal      # horizontal (default, zones L→R) | vertical (zones T→B)
35: 
36: zones:                       # 2..4 zones, ordered along the orientation axis
37:   - name: "COLLECTION"
38:     components:              # 1..5 components per zone
39:       - id: survey-solutions
40:         name: "Survey Solutions"
41:         sub:  "CAPI · PostgreSQL"
42:         icon: postgres               # any id from references/primitives/primitive-icons.md
43:         kind: standard               # standard | focal | external (external → dashed stroke)
44:       - { id: aspnet,    name: "ASP.NET Apps",    sub: "migration · admin portals", icon: server }
45:       - { id: civil-reg, name: "Civil Registry",  sub: "external · CRVS data",      icon: database, kind: external }
46:   - name: "PROCESSING"
47:     components:
48:       - { id: shared-drive,  name: "Shared Drive",     sub: "No version control · Windows file share", icon: file,      kind: focal }
49:       - { id: analyst-mach,  name: "Analyst Machines", sub: "SPSS · SAS · Stata · Excel",              icon: desktop }
50:       - { id: sql-server,    name: "SQL Server",       sub: "on-premises · core RDBMS",                icon: sqlserver, color: "#7a8c47" }  # custom olive
51:   - name: "DISSEMINATION"
52:     components:
53:       - { id: legacy-portal,   name: "LegacyPortal",      sub: "manual bottleneck",     icon: cloud,    kind: focal }
54:       - { id: natstat-website, name: "NatStat Website",   sub: "public · static pages", icon: internet }
55:       - { id: ministry,        name: "Ministry Partners", sub: "~6 ministries",         icon: users,    kind: external }
56: 
57: connectors:                   # ordered list; each links two component ids
58:   - { from: survey-solutions, to: shared-drive,   label: "CSV",     icon: csv,   style: link }
59:   - { from: aspnet,           to: shared-drive,   label: "EMAIL",   icon: file,  style: link }      # `mail` MISSING in catalog → falls back to `file`
60:   - { from: civil-reg,        to: shared-drive,   label: "EXCEL",   icon: excel, style: link, dashed: true }
61:   - { from: shared-drive,     to: analyst-mach,   label: "COPY",                 style: accent, dashed: true }
62:   - { from: analyst-mach,     to: sql-server,     label: "LOAD",                 style: neutral }
63:   - { from: analyst-mach,     to: legacy-portal,   label: "EXCEL",  icon: excel, style: accent }
64:   - { from: legacy-portal,    to: natstat-website, label: "WEB",                 style: neutral }
65:   - { from: natstat-website,  to: ministry,        label: "CSV DL", icon: csv,   style: link, dashed: true }
66: 
67: footer:                       # 0..3 optional full-canvas-width bars (cross-cutting concerns)
68:   - { name: "Identity Manager", sub: "Active Directory · LDAP · SSO", icon: active-directory }
69:   - { name: "Observability",    sub: "logs · metrics · alerts",       icon: monitoring }
70: 
71: legend:                       # auto-generated from styles used; user can override labels
72:   - { swatch: link,    label: "data flow" }
73:   - { swatch: accent,  label: "pain-point" }
74:   - { swatch: dashed,  label: "external" }
75:   - { swatch: focal,   label: "bottleneck" }
76: 
77: dark: false
78: ```
79: 
80: **Reserved field semantics:**
81: 
82: - `orientation` — `horizontal` (zones run L→R, components stack vertically inside each zone) or `vertical` (zones stack T→B, components run L→R inside each zone).
83: - `zones[i].name` — uppercase short label (≤ 14 chars). Rendered at the top-left of the zone box in the `eyebrow` role with letter-spacing 0.14em, on a paper-masked break in the zone border.
84: - `components[i][k].id` — globally unique slug; referenced by `connectors[].from/to`.
85: - `components[i][k].name` — `node-name` role (the human-readable label).
86: - `components[i][k].sub` — `sublabel` role at 10px in muted (the technical sub-label; up to 2 lines via auto-wrap when component height grows to 72).
87: - `components[i][k].icon` — any id from `references/primitives/primitive-icons.md`. If missing → no icon, the name shifts left. (Catalog has 41 icons; `mail` is currently missing — use `icon: file` as fallback for email hand-offs.)
88: - `components[i][k].kind` — `standard | focal | external`. `focal` triggers the accent palette (§6); `external` switches to a 4-2 dashed stroke and muted ink to signal "this is outside our scope."
89: - `components[i][k].color` — optional per-component color override (§5). Ignored on `kind: focal` (accent wins).
90: - `connectors[k].from` / `connectors[k].to` — refer to a component `id`. Cross-zone, cross-row, same-zone vertical, and same-zone horizontal all legal; routing chosen by §4.
91: - `connectors[k].label` — uppercase short text (≤ 8 chars). `arrow-label` role at 9px, weight 600.
92: - `connectors[k].icon` — optional inline icon to the left of the text. Same catalog as component icons.
93: - `connectors[k].style` — `neutral | link | accent`. Drives stroke color + marker.
94: - `connectors[k].dashed` — `true | false`.
95: - `footer[k]` — optional cross-cutting bar. Spans full canvas width minus margins. No connectors drawn from a footer.
96: - `legend[k].swatch` — `link | accent | dashed | focal | neutral`. Auto-curated based on what the diagram actually uses; user can re-order or rename.
97: 
98: ---
99: 
100: ## 3. LAYOUT FORMULAS — DETERMINISTIC GEOMETRY
101: 
102: ```
103: # Horizontal orientation (default)
104: left_pad        = 16
105: right_pad       = 16
106: zone_gap        = 20
107: zone_y          = 52
108: zone_h          = 360
109: n_zones         = len(zones)
110: 
111: # Zone widths: base 200 + 24 per component to give vertical room for icons + 2-line subs.
112: # In the canonical example (3 / 3 / 3 components) the replication used 256 / 360 / 272 —
113: # the formula approximates that with hand-picked widths in the worked YAML (§11).
114: zone_w(i)       = base + n_components_i * comp_slack             # base ≈ 200, slack ≈ 24
115: viewBox_w       = left_pad + Σ zone_w(i) + (n_zones-1) * zone_gap + right_pad
116: 
117: # Component placement within zone i
118: comp_pad_x      = 20                                              # x-inset from zone border
119: comp_h          = 56                                              # 68 for focal (2-line sub), 72 if both sub lines present
120: comp_gap        = 32
121: comp_y(i, k)    = zone_y + 28 + k * (comp_h + comp_gap)
122: 
123: # Component centerlines (used for connector routing)
124: comp_x(i)       = zone_x(i) + comp_pad_x
125: comp_w(i)       = zone_w(i) - 2 * comp_pad_x
126: comp_cx(i)      = comp_x(i) + comp_w(i)/2
127: comp_cy(i, k)   = comp_y(i, k) + comp_h/2
128: 
129: # Footer bars (if present)
130: footer_bar_h    = 56
131: footer_gap      = 8
132: footer_top      = zone_y + zone_h + 24
133: footer_y(k)     = footer_top + k * (footer_bar_h + footer_gap)
134: footer_bottom   = footer_top + N_footer * (footer_bar_h + footer_gap) - footer_gap
135: 
136: # Total canvas height
137: legend_block_h  = 40
138: content_bottom  = N_footer > 0 ? footer_bottom : zone_y + zone_h
139: viewBox_h       = content_bottom + legend_block_h + 24
140: ```
141: 
142: ### 3.1 Background and zone frame
143: 
144: Solid paper fill across `viewBox`. No dot pattern. Each zone box:
145: 
146: ```svg
147: <rect x="zone_x(i)" y="zone_y" width="zone_w(i)" height="zone_h"
148:       fill="{ink @ 0.02}" stroke="{ink @ 0.10}" stroke-width="0.8" rx="8"/>
149: <!-- paper-masked break for the zone label -->
150: <rect x="zone_x(i)+20" y="zone_y-8" width="{label_w}" height="16" fill="{paper}"/>
151: <text x="zone_x(i)+24" y="zone_y+4" fill="{ink @ 0.40}"
152:       font-family="{eyebrow}" letter-spacing="0.14em">{name}</text>
153: ```
154: 
155: ### 3.2 Component box
156: 
157: Three visual kinds:
158: 
159: | `kind` | Fill | Stroke | Stroke width | Stroke dash | Name ink | Sub ink |
160: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
161: | `standard` | `#FFFFFF` | `ink` | 1 | — | `ink` | `muted` |
162: | `focal` | `accent @ 0.07` | `accent` | 1.4 | — | `ink` | `accent` (line 1) + `muted` (line 2) |
163: | `external` | `#FFFFFF` | `muted` | 1 | `4,3` | `ink` | `muted` |
164: 
165: **Icon placement** (24×24, monochrome via `currentColor` — see `references/primitives/primitive-icons.md`):
166: 
167: ```svg
168: <g transform="translate(comp_x + 12, comp_y + (comp_h - 24)/2)" color="{ink_for_kind}">
169:   <use href="#icon-{name}"/>            <!-- or inline the SVG path from the catalog -->
170: </g>
171: ```
172: 
173: Icon takes 24 × 24 → 36-px total horizontal footprint with the 12-px left pad. Name and sub-label baseline shifts right by 40 px.
174: 
175: **Name + sub baselines** (left-aligned, with icon to the left):
176: 
177: ```
178: name_x = comp_x + 44
179: name_y = comp_y + (comp_h/2) - 2
180: sub_y  = comp_y + (comp_h/2) + 14
181: ```
182: 
183: ### 3.3 Connector geometry (§4 holds the routing rules)
184: 
185: ```
186: src_right  = comp_x(i_src) + comp_w(i_src)
187: src_left   = comp_x(i_src)
188: src_top    = comp_y(i_src, k_src)
189: src_bot    = src_top + comp_h_src
190: src_cy     = src_top + comp_h_src/2
191: 
192: dst_left   = comp_x(i_dst)
193: dst_right  = comp_x(i_dst) + comp_w(i_dst)
194: dst_top    = comp_y(i_dst, k_dst)
195: dst_bot    = dst_top + comp_h_dst
196: dst_cx     = comp_cx(i_dst)
197: dst_cy     = dst_top + comp_h_dst/2
198: 
199: # Corridor x for cross-zone H+Q+V routing
200: corridor_x = dst_cx                            # land arrow on dst horizontal center, enter via top/bot
201: ```
202: 
203: ### 3.4 Footer bar
204: 
205: ```svg
206: <rect x="left_pad" y="footer_y(k)" width="viewBox_w - 2*left_pad" height="footer_bar_h"
207:       fill="{ink @ 0.03}" stroke="{ink @ 0.18}" stroke-width="0.8" rx="8"/>
208: <g transform="translate(left_pad + 20, footer_y(k) + (footer_bar_h - 24)/2)" color="{ink}">
209:   <use href="#icon-{name}"/>
210: </g>
211: <text x="left_pad + 56" y="footer_y(k) + 24" font-family="{node-name}" font-size="14" fill="{ink}">{name}</text>
212: <text x="left_pad + 56" y="footer_y(k) + 40" font-family="{sublabel}" font-size="12" fill="{muted}">{sub}</text>
213: ```
214: 
215: Footer bars are layer-wide services. **No connectors emerge from them.** They sit visually below the zones and let the reader see the cross-cutting concerns at a glance.
216: 
217: ### 3.5 Legend strip
218: 
219: Hairline divider at `y = content_bottom + 16`, then a row of swatches + labels at `y = content_bottom + 36`. Only the styles actually used by `connectors[]` (plus `focal` and `external` if those component kinds are present) appear in the legend.
220: 
221: ---
222: 
223: ## 4. CONNECTOR RULES (MANDATORY)
224: 
225: ### 4.1 Path shape — rounded right-angle Q-bezier, r = 8
226: 
227: Reused verbatim from `type-process.md` §4.1. No diagonals — ever.
228: 
229: ```svg
230: <!-- Same zone, adjacent component (same vertical column): single vertical line -->
231: <line x1="{src_cx}" y1="{src_bot}" x2="{dst_cx}" y2="{dst_top}"
232:       stroke="…" stroke-width="…" marker-end="…"/>
233: 
234: <!-- Cross-zone or cross-row: exit right → H → Q-bend → V → enter top (or bottom) -->
235: <path d="M {src_right},{src_cy}  H {dst_cx - 8}  Q {dst_cx},{src_cy} {dst_cx},{src_cy ± 8}  V {dst_top_or_bottom}"
236:       fill="none" stroke="…" stroke-width="…" marker-end="…"/>
237: ```
238: 
239: - Use `{src_cy + 8}` and `V {dst_top}` when destination lies BELOW source.
240: - Use `{src_cy − 8}` and `V {dst_bottom}` when destination lies ABOVE source.
241: 
242: ### 4.2 Exit / entry sides (configurable; defaults below)
243: 
244: | Topology | Default exit side of source | Default entry side of destination |
245: | --- | --- | --- |
246: | Same zone, dst below | bottom | top |
247: | Same zone, dst above | top | bottom |
248: | Cross-zone, horizontal flow | right | top (or bottom, whichever is closer to src_cy) |
249: | Vertical-orientation diagram | bottom | top |
250: 
251: A connector can override via `connectors[k].from_side` / `connectors[k].to_side` (`top | right | bottom | left`). **Backward references** (right→left in horizontal orientation, up in vertical orientation) are permitted only when at least one endpoint has `kind: external`, and must be `dashed: true`.
252: 
253: ### 4.3 Markers MUST touch the destination rectangle
254: 
255: The path's last command ends at the destination's rectangle edge (`V {dst_top}` or `H {dst_left}`), **not** at the centroid. After applying `refX=7` on the marker, the triangle sits flush against the border. Stopping the line short of the edge — or sending it to the centroid and burying the arrowhead inside the rect — is a hard fail.
256: 
257: ### 4.4 Style → stroke + marker
258: 
259: | `style` | Stroke color | Stroke width | Marker |
260: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
261: | `neutral` | `muted` | 1.0 | `url(#arrow)` |
262: | `link` | `link` | 1.2 | `url(#arrow-link)` |
263: | `accent` | `accent` | 1.4 | `url(#arrow-accent)` |
264: 
265: Add `stroke-dasharray="4 3"` when `dashed: true`.
266: 
267: **Defs block** (always emit all three):
268: 
269: ```svg
270: <defs>
271:   <marker id="arrow"        markerWidth="8" markerHeight="6" refX="7" refY="3" orient="auto"><polygon points="0 0, 8 3, 0 6" fill="{muted}"/></marker>
272:   <marker id="arrow-link"   markerWidth="8" markerHeight="6" refX="7" refY="3" orient="auto"><polygon points="0 0, 8 3, 0 6" fill="{link}"/></marker>
273:   <marker id="arrow-accent" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="6" refX="7" refY="3" orient="auto"><polygon points="0 0, 8 3, 0 6" fill="{accent}"/></marker>
274: </defs>
275: ```
276: 
277: ### 4.5 Connector label = inline icon + text, placed at the START of the connector with a perpendicular margin
278: 
279: The label sits **near the source end** of the connector (not at the mid-segment) and is **offset perpendicular to the line** so it never overlaps the stroke. Icon (when `icon:` is set) sits inside the label's paper-fill mask, to the left of the text.
280: 
281: ```svg
282: <g transform="translate({label_cx}, {label_cy})">
283:   <rect x="-{w/2}" y="-9" width="{w}" height="18" rx="3" fill="{paper}" stroke="none"/>
284:   <use href="#icon-{icon}" x="-{w/2 + 4}" y="-6" width="12" height="12" color="{stroke_color}"/>     <!-- if icon set -->
285:   <text x="{icon ? (-(w/2) + 22) : 0}" y="3" text-anchor="{icon ? 'start' : 'middle'}"
286:         font-family="{arrow-label}" font-size="9" font-weight="600"
287:         letter-spacing="0.08em" fill="{stroke_color}">{label}</text>
288: </g>
289: ```
290: 
291: **Placement formulas** (label box is 18px tall × `w` wide; centered on `{label_cx, label_cy}`):
292: 
293: | Segment exiting source | `label_cx` | `label_cy` | Effect |
294: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
295: | Horizontal (right exit) | `src_right + 6 + w/2` | `src_cy − 14` | Label sits 6 px past the source, 5 px above the line |
296: | Horizontal (left exit, backward) | `src_left − 6 − w/2` | `src_cy − 14` | Label sits 6 px before the source, 5 px above the line |
297: | Vertical (bottom exit) | `src_cx + 6 + w/2` | `src_bot + 14` | Label sits 6 px right of the line, 5 px below the source edge |
298: | Vertical (top exit, backward) | `src_cx + 6 + w/2` | `src_top − 14` | Label sits 6 px right of the line, 5 px above the source edge |
299: 
300: For cross-zone H+Q+V routes the label binds to the **horizontal** segment, since that segment is anchored at the source. Place the label early on that horizontal run — never on the Q-bend or the vertical tail.
301: 
302: - `w = text_w + (icon ? 30 : 12)` — auto-fit.
303: - Mask `fill` resolves to `paper` in light mode and `ink` in dark mode. The mask is kept as a safety pad — even though the label no longer sits on the line, it can graze zone backgrounds and component fills, and the mask preserves contrast.
304: - `stroke_color` follows §4.4 (text + icon inherit the connector's accent / link / neutral color).
305: 
306: ### 4.6 Z-order
307: 
308: All connectors (paths + lines + labels) emit BEFORE any component rect, so node fills mask the line ends. The connector label is the exception — it draws AFTER its line so the mask sits on top.
309: 
310: ---
311: 
312: ## 5. COMPONENT COLOR OVERRIDE (PER-COMPONENT `color: "#hex"`)
313: 
314: Per-component, same shape as every other parametric type in this skill.
315: 
316: | Element | Light | Dark |
317: | --- | --- | --- |
318: | Container fill | `rgba(C, 0.06)` | `rgba(C_light, 0.10)` |
319: | Container stroke | `rgba(C, 0.45)` (width 1) | `rgba(C_light, 0.55)` |
320: | Component name text | `C` | `C_light` |
321: | Icon glyph | inherits ink via `currentColor` (unchanged) | inherits ink (unchanged) |
322: | Sub-label | muted (unchanged) | muted (unchanged) |
323: | Connectors touching this component | **unchanged** — topology-driven | **unchanged** |
324: 
325: `C_light` = the same hex lightened ~15 % for dark-mode contrast (e.g., `#7a8c47` → `#9aac67`, `#b85450` → `#d97a78`).
326: 
327: **Rules:**
328: - **Never on focal components.** `kind: focal` always renders accent; `color` is silently ignored.
329: - **Never on connectors.** Connector style is topology-driven; if you want a colored edge, pick `style: accent` / `link` / `neutral`, not a component color.
330: - **Cap: ≤ 3 custom-colored components per diagram** (in addition to focal components). Above 3 the visual signal fragments.
331: 
332: **Recommended cross-type palette** (same as `type-medallion.md` / `type-process.md` / `type-dp-integration.md` / `type-dp-security-matrix.md`):
333: 
334: - `#b85450` rust-red — security / governance / pain-point that isn't focal
335: - `#5a7d9a` slate-blue — observability / quality / monitoring gate
336: - `#7a8c47` olive-green — survivor system (the one tool the new platform keeps)
337: - `#c9a23a` warm yellow — sandbox / dev / scratch
338: - `#8c6d3f` warm-brown — archive / cold / DR
339: 
340: ---
341: 
342: ## 6. FOCAL RULE
343: 
344: - `kind: focal` components: **≤ 2 per diagram** (zero is also valid for diagrams without a single dominant pain-point).
345: - Auto-styling: accent stroke 1.4, accent-tinted fill 7 %, ink-bold `node-name`, accent line-1 `sublabel`.
346: - Any connector with a focal endpoint automatically renders in `style: accent`; the YAML `style:` is ignored.
347: - Custom `color: "#hex"` on a focal component is silently ignored — accent always wins.
348: 
349: If your diagram needs more than 2 focal components, you've collapsed two narratives. Split: one "collection pain-points" diagram + one "dissemination pain-points" diagram.
350: 
351: ---
352: 
353: ## 7. DARK MODE
354: 
355: | Role | Light | Dark |
356: | --- | --- | --- |
357: | paper | `paper` | `ink` |
358: | ink | `ink` | `paper` |
359: | muted | `muted` | `muted` |
360: | accent | `accent` | `accent` |
361: | link | `link` | `link` |
362: | zone background | `ink @ 0.02` | `paper @ 0.04` |
363: | zone border | `ink @ 0.10` | `paper @ 0.14` |
364: | standard component fill | `#FFFFFF` | `paper @ 0.04` |
365: | standard component stroke | `ink` | `paper @ 0.32` |
366: | focal fill | `accent @ 0.07` | `accent @ 0.12` |
367: | focal stroke | `accent` | `accent` |
368: | external stroke | `muted` (dashed) | `muted` (dashed) |
369: | footer fill | `ink @ 0.03` | `paper @ 0.05` |
370: | footer stroke | `ink @ 0.18` | `paper @ 0.20` |
371: | label mask fill | `paper` | `ink` |
372: | custom-color components | `C` | `C_light` (≈ +15 %) |
373: 
374: ---
375: 
376: ## 8. REPRODUCIBILITY CHECKLIST (TASTE GATE)
377: 
378: Before emitting SVG, verify **every** item:
379: 
380: 1. Eyebrow + title + subtitle present at canonical y-positions (24 / 36 / 52); body padding 32 px.
381: 2. 2..4 zones; each has its uppercase label at the top-left of its zone box, on a paper-masked break in the border.
382: 3. Every component has `id`, `name`. `sub`, `icon`, `kind`, `color` are optional.
383: 4. ≤ 2 components with `kind: focal`; focal styling auto-applied (accent fill 7 %, accent stroke 1.4, italic line-1 sub).
384: 5. Every connector exits the right (or bottom) of source and enters the top (or left) of destination; rounded right-angle Q-bezier `r=8` at every bend; marker triangle visibly touches the destination rectangle edge.
385: 6. Connector labels sit at the **start** of the connector (not mid-segment) and are offset **perpendicular** to the line (5 px gap above for horizontal segments, 6 px gap to the right for vertical segments) — never overlapping the stroke. Paper-fill mask kept behind text; icon (when `icon:` is set) sits left of text inside the same mask.
386: 7. ≤ 3 custom-colored components; none on focal.
387: 8. ≤ 3 footer bars; each spans `viewBox_w − 2*left_pad`; no connectors emerge from any footer.
388: 9. Legend at bottom: hairline separator + one swatch per style actually used.
389: 10. `arrow-label` for connector labels, `eyebrow` for the page eyebrow and zone labels, `title` for the page title, `node-name` for the subtitle and component names, and `sublabel` for technical sub-labels.
390: 11. Markers `#arrow` / `#arrow-link` / `#arrow-accent` defined once in `<defs>`; no inline marker definitions.
391: 12. Dark variant: resolve every semantic token through its dark-mode value; custom colors are lightened ~15 %.
392: 
393: ---
394: 
395: ## 9. ANTI-PATTERNS
396: 
397: - **Diagonal arrows.** The NatStat replication has one (analyst → LegacyPortal). The new type forbids it — always rounded right-angle Q-bezier.
398: - **Marker not touching the target.** Path ends at the centroid or stops short of the border.
399: - **Inline `text` connector labels without a mask rect.** The connector line can bleed through the text and it becomes unreadable.
400: - **Labels sitting on top of the connector line, mid-segment.** Labels belong at the *start* of the connector with a perpendicular margin (see §4.5) — burying them in the middle of the line hides the source-to-destination direction and forces the reader's eye to fight the mask.
401: - **Tiny text badges as icons.** The source uses 7-px `DB` / `APP` / `EXT` badges; this type uses real 24-px catalog icons. Text badges are only acceptable as the label text, not as the component "icon."
402: - **Custom color on a focal component.** Focal always wins; user-set `color` silently ignored on `kind: focal`.
403: - **Footer bar wired to one component.** Footer = cross-cutting layer-wide concern; a connector from a footer to a specific component is a category error (use `type-dp-integration.md`'s AUTH-line pattern only when the footer service truly authenticates *all* components, and even then the line lands at the zone bottom edge, not at a specific tool).
404: - **> 16 total components or > 5 per zone.** Density cap; split into two diagrams.
405: - **Mixing orientations within one diagram.** Pick one — `horizontal` or `vertical` — and apply it to every zone.
406: - **Using `kind: focal` to flag every painful thing.** Focal exists for ≤ 2 narrative pain-points; for "this is bad but not headline-bad", use `color: "#b85450"` rust-red instead.
407: 
408: ---
409: 
410: ## 10. EXAMPLES
411: 
412: - `assets/diagrams/it-state.html` — minimal light (NatStat canonical: 3 zones, 9 components, 8 connectors, 0 footer bars, SQL Server tinted olive). Gallery default.
413: - `assets/diagrams/it-state-dark.html` — same, dark skin.
414: - `assets/diagrams/it-state-full.html` — same, editorial-card frame with summary cards.
415: - `assets/diagrams/it-state-extended.html` — exercises §5 color override + footer bars: 2 footer bars (Identity Manager + Observability) below the zones, third custom color on Analyst Machines (slate-blue, data-quality concern).
416: - `assets/diagrams/it-state-extended-dark.html` — extended pattern, dark skin.
417: 
418: ---
419: 
420: ## 11. WORKED YAML — FULL INPUTS FOR `it-state.html`
421: 
422: The complete inputs that map to the shipped canonical example. Every coordinate in that SVG is derivable from §3 applied to these inputs.
423: 
424: ```yaml
425: title:    "Current IT Landscape"
426: subtitle: "Data pipeline before the platform"
427: eyebrow:  "NatStat · Before the platform"
428: 
429: orientation: horizontal
430: 
431: zones:
432:   - name: "COLLECTION"
433:     components:
434:       - { id: survey-solutions, name: "Survey Solutions", sub: "CAPI · PostgreSQL",          icon: postgres }
435:       - { id: aspnet,           name: "ASP.NET Apps",     sub: "migration · admin portals", icon: server   }
436:       - { id: civil-reg,        name: "Civil Registry",   sub: "external · CRVS data",      icon: database, kind: external }
437:   - name: "PROCESSING"
438:     components:
439:       - { id: shared-drive,  name: "Shared Drive",     sub: "No version control · Windows file share", icon: file,      kind: focal }
440:       - { id: analyst-mach,  name: "Analyst Machines", sub: "SPSS · SAS · Stata · Excel",              icon: desktop }
441:       - { id: sql-server,    name: "SQL Server",       sub: "on-premises · core RDBMS",                icon: sqlserver, color: "#7a8c47" }
442:   - name: "DISSEMINATION"
443:     components:
444:       - { id: legacy-portal,   name: "LegacyPortal",      sub: "manual bottleneck",     icon: cloud,    kind: focal }
445:       - { id: natstat-website, name: "NatStat Website",   sub: "public · static pages", icon: internet }
446:       - { id: ministry,        name: "Ministry Partners", sub: "~6 ministries",         icon: users,    kind: external }
447: 
448: connectors:
449:   - { from: survey-solutions, to: shared-drive,   label: "CSV",    icon: csv,   style: link }
450:   - { from: aspnet,           to: shared-drive,   label: "EMAIL",  icon: file,  style: link }
451:   - { from: civil-reg,        to: shared-drive,   label: "EXCEL",  icon: excel, style: link, dashed: true }
452:   - { from: shared-drive,     to: analyst-mach,   label: "COPY",                style: accent, dashed: true }
453:   - { from: analyst-mach,     to: sql-server,     label: "LOAD",                style: neutral }
454:   - { from: analyst-mach,     to: legacy-portal,   label: "EXCEL",  icon: excel, style: accent }
455:   - { from: legacy-portal,    to: natstat-website, label: "WEB",                 style: neutral }
456:   - { from: natstat-website,  to: ministry,        label: "CSV DL", icon: csv,   style: link, dashed: true }
457: 
458: dark: false
459: ```
460: 
461: ### 11.1 What this YAML proves
462: 
463: - `n_zones = 3`, components per zone `= [3, 3, 3]`, custom color count = 1 (SQL Server), focal count = 2 (Shared Drive, LegacyPortal), external count = 2 (Civil Registry, Ministry Partners).
464: - Zone widths in canonical: 256 / 360 / 272 ⇒ `viewBox_w = 16 + 256 + 20 + 360 + 20 + 272 + 16 = 960` ✓
465: - `viewBox_h = 52 + 360 + 40 + 24 = 500` (no footer bars) ✓
466: - Shared Drive (focal) at zone 2, row 0: `x = 340, y = 80, w = 264, h = 68` (focal stretches to 68 to fit 2-line sub) ✓
467: - LegacyPortal (focal) at zone 3, row 0: `x = 704, y = 80, w = 208, h = 60` ✓
468: - SQL Server (custom olive) at zone 2, row 2: container fill `rgba(122,140,71,0.06)`, stroke `rgba(122,140,71,0.45)`, name text `#7a8c47` ✓
469: - Connectors 4, 5 (within zone 2) and 7, 8 (within zone 3) are simple vertical `<line>` elements. Cross-zone connectors take rule-compliant routes (see SKILL.md §4 rules 14 & 15):
470:   - **All three Survey-side → Shared Drive connectors (C1 / C2 / C3) enter Shared Drive's LEFT edge.** A top-edge entry would push the marker body (7 px back along travel, given `refX = 7`) *inside* the destination box, where the box's paper-fill mask hides it — only a 1-pixel tip would peek above the stroke. Entering the left edge with a right-going path keeps the body outside the box and the arrow visible (~7 px shown to the left of the box edge). The three left-edge attach points are fanned at **y = 108 / 124 / 140** (16-px spacing, well above the 12 px rule 14 minimum).
471:   - **C1** (Survey → Shared Drive) source y matches landing y: single horizontal `M 252,108 H 340`. No bends needed.
472:   - **C2** (ASP.NET → Shared Drive) detours up through zone-2 background — vertical at `x = 316` (clear of Shared Drive's left edge at `x = 340`): `H 308 Q 316,196 316,188 V 132 Q 316,124 324,124 H 340`. Lands at `(340, 124)`.
473:   - **C3** (Civil Registry → Shared Drive) detours up through zone-2 background — vertical at `x = 332` (clear of Analyst Machines, which starts at `x = 340`): `H 324 Q 332,284 332,276 V 148 Q 332,140 340,140`. Lands at `(340, 140)` via a final Q-bend (no trailing H needed).
474:   - **C6** (Analyst Machines → LegacyPortal) cannot use a direct H+Q+V into LegacyPortal's left edge — Analyst Machines and LegacyPortal are in different rows, and the direct horizontal at `y = 268` would cross NatStat Website. It detours through the zone gap and **over** LegacyPortal: `H 654 Q 662,268 662,260 V 72 Q 662,64 670,64 H 800 Q 808,64 808,72 V 80` — vertical at `x = 662` (in zone gap), horizontal at `y = 64` (above LegacyPortal top), then down into LegacyPortal's top center. The path enters LegacyPortal from **above** going down, so the arrow body lives above the box (visible) and only the 1-px tip enters the box.
475: 
476: **Marker-visibility rule of thumb:** with the standard arrow marker (`markerWidth = 8`, `refX = 7`), the arrow body extends 7 px *backwards* along the path direction from the endpoint. For the arrow to remain visible, that 7-px tail must sit *outside* the destination box. Translation:
477: - Entering a **TOP edge going UP** (path direction up, box below) → body inside box, **only 1 px visible. Avoid this.**
478: - Entering a **TOP edge going DOWN** (path direction down, box below) → body above box, ~7 px visible. ✓
479: - Entering a **LEFT edge going RIGHT** → body to the left of box, ~7 px visible. ✓
480: - Entering a **RIGHT edge going LEFT** → body to the right of box, ~7 px visible. ✓
481: - Entering a **BOTTOM edge going DOWN** (box above) → body inside box, **only 1 px visible. Avoid this.**
482: - Entering a **BOTTOM edge going UP** (box above) → body below box, ~7 px visible. ✓
483: 
484: When the source row matches the destination row's y range (e.g., Survey at y=108 with Shared Drive at y=80–148), prefer **side-edge** entry — a single horizontal path with a fully visible arrow. When the source row is offset, detour through the destination's nearest zone background to enter a side edge rather than approaching a top/bottom edge from the wrong side.
485: 
486: The extended example (§10 line 4) demonstrates footer bars + a third custom color and proves `viewBox_h` grows correctly when `N_footer > 0`.

15: # Line Chart
16: 
17: ## 1. OVERVIEW
18: 
19: **Best for:** continuous trends over time or a sequential index — signups over weeks, revenue by month, latency over releases. Use when the direction and rate of change between points is the primary message.
20: 
21: ---
22: 
23: ## 2. LAYOUT CONVENTIONS
24: 
25: - **Plot area margins:** left 80px, bottom 60px, top 40px, right 40px — inside `0 0 1000 500` viewBox.
26: - **Points:** 4–12 data points. Fewer → consider a summary stat; more → aggregate into periods.
27: - **X-axis:** evenly spaced time/index labels below the plot. Use Geist Mono 8px, centered on each point x.
28: - **Y-axis gridlines:** 4–6 horizontals at regular intervals. Same faint treatment as bar chart.
29: - **Lines:** `<polyline>` with `fill="none"`. Focal series `stroke-width="1.8"`, others `"1.2"`.
30: - **Vertex dots:** only on the focal series (`r=4`, filled). Other series: line only.
31: - **Area fill (optional):** `<polygon>` closing back to `y=420` (x-axis baseline) at 0.08 opacity. Use for the focal series only when the area meaning is important.
32: - **Multi-series:** up to 5 series. Focal = `accent`. Others = `series-1`, `series-2`, `series-3`, `series-4` from style-guide.md. Apply series palette in order — don't skip.
33: - **Legend:** horizontal strip at the bottom. Swatch = 16×8px rect with the series fill/stroke. One entry per series.
34: 
35: ### Polyline pattern
36: 
37: ```svg
38: <!-- Focal series -->
39: <polyline points="x0,y0 x1,y1 x2,y2 ..."
40:           fill="none" stroke="#eb6c36" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-linejoin="round"/>
41: <!-- Dots at each point (focal only) -->
42: <circle cx="x0" cy="y0" r="4" fill="#eb6c36"/>
43: 
44: <!-- Non-focal series -->
45: <polyline points="x0,y0 x1,y1 ..."
46:           fill="none" stroke="#7c8f6f" stroke-width="1.2" stroke-linejoin="round"/>
47: ```
48: 
49: ---
50: 
51: ## 3. ANTI-PATTERNS
52: 
53: - More than 5 series (visual mush — reduce or split).
54: - Lines that don't start at a shared zero baseline unless explicitly annotated.
55: - Smoothed/spline curves when the underlying data is sampled — polyline is honest.
56: - Dots on every series when there are 4+ series (only focal gets dots).
57: - Y-axis that doesn't include zero when the absolute magnitude matters.
58: - Connecting discontinuous data segments without a visual gap.
59: 
60: ---
61: 
62: ## 4. EXAMPLES
63: 
64: - `assets/diagrams/line.html` — minimal light
65: - `assets/diagrams/line-dark.html` — minimal dark
66: - `assets/diagrams/line-full.html` — full editorial
